#2743. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

"Although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously announced commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.

The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

Tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

It's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The company had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

CoreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, said CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

"We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

"However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person."

"There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us."

Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

The real issue is just how much money the company will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

"Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he said. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies."

— CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

#2742. Spain test will reveal if Tuchel and England have learned World Cup lessons

England's proof of progress and the lessons learned by head coach Thomas Tuchel since the disappointment of World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina will be put to the sternest test when they face holders Spain in Madrid.

Spain present the toughest assignment England could face, with the world champions' unbeaten run – in which they claimed the sport's biggest prize by beating Argentina in New Jersey in the summer – now stretching to 43 games.

Luis de la Fuente's side last lost - to Colombia - in March 2024, winning 34 games and drawing nine in the intervening period, during which they also became European champions, beating England in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin.

Little wonder, then, that England captain and Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane describes Sunday night's visit to the Metropolitano Stadium as: "The perfect opportunity to try and prove ourselves."

Tuchel, who revealed Leeds United's James Trafford will get another opportunity in goal as he continues to alternate with Jordan Pickford, clearly feels the same as he added: "This will be proof of concept on the highest level. It's the biggest test in world football. Spain are unbelievable on an incredible run.

"Spain won the last big titles. We are trying to take it away from them. We are up for it. We are in a good moment to push our limits. We are up for something spectacular."

It was a message echoed here in Madrid by England midfielder Declan Rice, who said: "It's a massive game.

"I don't think you can get much bigger than a Champions League final with Arsenal or a World Cup semi-final against Argentina, which I've played in, but when you are playing against the world champions in Spain there is no greater incentive.

"It's the sort of game that brings out the best in us. We want to play against the best teams and the best players. It will show where we are as a group. We're going to see where England are at."

Spain are particularly formidable on home soil, unbeaten in 20 games - winning 15 and drawing five - since a 2-1 defeat by Switzerland in September 2022.

England's most recent win in Spain was a 3-2 triumph in a Nations League encounter in Sevilla in October 2018, their first away victory against them for 31 years.

Yet England came closer than most to piercing Spain's air of invincibility, even though they lost 3-2 at Wembley in September, when a rare Kane blemish from the penalty spot prevented them taking a potentially decisive 3-1 lead.

Spain subsequently punished England and Kane, who will be hoping for better fortunes when the countries meet again in the latest Nations League encounter.

England arrived in Madrid on Saturday evening having reeled off four successive victories since that Wembley loss, the latest of which was a 2-1 win against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday.

Spain will present an altogether different opposition, but also a barometer of whether England have moved forward since the World Cup, when Tuchel was heavily criticised for what was perceived to be a negative approach in the 2-1 loss to Argentina in Atlanta, especially after Anthony Gordon put England ahead.

Former England defender Matthew Upson, who will be in Madrid for BBC Radio 5 Live, told BBC Sport: "Harry Kane saying this is the perfect opportunity for England to prove themselves is a great way to build this challenge up.

"I wouldn't expect anything less from him considering where he is at now, where his belief level is and what he wants to achieve.

"Harry is achieving incredible personal accolades like the Ballon d'Or, but he won't rest there. He will want a team honour with England, and if you play against the best in the world there is no better barometer of where you're at as a group.

"It's going to be a very interesting test. It's fair to say we didn't see England at full flow against Croatia, so now we will see if they adjust, improve and produce something of their best, which they will have to do if you are going to get any sort of result against Spain in Spain.

"If England get a point, or even better a win, against Spain with their record, at home and away, we will come away thinking they are at a high level.

"If you get a result, you will have had to play really well because you won't do that with anything else.

"By that, I don't mean a blistering game. I just mean doing things well and showing the level you are at."

In the aftermath of that World Cup loss to Argentina, the post-tournament process embarked upon by the Football Asssociation included canvassing the opinions of the whole squad, where it emerged it took place at a "full and frank" meeting with Tuchel at the start of the September international break.

Kane and Jude Bellingham were understood to have given forthright views, where the approach in the devastating loss to Argentina was a key theme.

There is now believed to be a feeling in the squad that Tuchel has taken on the lessons of Atlanta and is focusing on a more positive approach.

Spain won Euro 2024 and this year's World Cup [Getty Images]

Upson said: "England are still a bit of a work in progress. We have two or maybe three players who are playing some of the best football across Europe and the world at the moment. I am thinking of Kane, Bellingham and, at times, Anthony Gordon.

"The key is utilising that, then getting the rest of the team to a place where it can support that and deliver its own world-class support. This is the challenge for Thomas Tuchel."

"England are adopting a more positive approach, but look a little vulnerable defensively, which is maybe the compromise.

"Yes, England could have been 3-1 up against Spain had Harry Kane scored his penalty, but don't forget we could easily have been 3-0 down before we scored."

The intense environment of facing the World Cup holders on their own turf will also be a forensic examination of England's mental progress as well as footballing prowess.

Upson said: "The biggest thing to fix after the World Cup was player reaction and player belief when we're in certain situations, especially if we go ahead and all of a sudden the game is difficult, as it was against Argentina. What is our mindset going to be?

"Since then England have tried to play much more freely, openly and confidently. That's how I see it. That's how we played when we won 7-0 in Croatia. We were free, open, positive. Belief was through the roof.

"This is why this test against Spain is great because you will get tested to the maximum there. If England go ahead, let's see how they do and what they do. If they go behind, let's see what we do.

"Against Spain at Wembley, I saw a reaction at half-time from England, which was fantastic. We should have gone 3-1 up with Harry's penalty, and in that 15 minutes after half-time we were super positive, aggressive in our decision-making.

"This was another ideal situation to test that. They came through that really positively. It would be great if we get another test like that on Sunday.

"It it all plays into what Harry Kane said. This is something which will test people. It's a really significant game for England on a lot of levels."

#2741. Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

(See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.)

Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

First, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout quickly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

Zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three important forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:

This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

The following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

The major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

One important clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

Any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

From here, it's all about the follow through.  We don't need to see new highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

Frank Cappelleri is the founder and president of CappThesis, an independent research firm that helps active investors through time-tested chart and statistical analysis. Prior to starting CappThesis, he spent 25 years on Wall Street as an equity sales trader, technical analyst, research sales specialist and desk strategist.

#2740. Lutnick faces questions over Nvidia spy scandal. His sons' firm has deep ties to the chipmaker

In late September, Cantor Fitzgerald hosted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other top executives from the chipmaker for investor meetings in New York, according to a Cantor research report reviewed by CNBC.

The Wall Street firm liked what it heard.

"We continue to view NVDA as the best risk/reward in our coverage," Cantor analyst C.J. Muse and his colleagues wrote in a research report dated Oct. 3 that maintained a $350 price target and overweight rating on the stock.

Yet the firm, formerly run by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and now led by his sons, Brandon and Kyle, reported a nearly 50% decline in the number of Nvidia shares it held between September 2025 and March 2026, according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings that excludes options. Nvidia had been one of the largest stock positions reported in Cantor's filings.

The decline coincided with White House and U.S. intelligence officials pressing Lutnick to crack down on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence chips to China. Lutnick repeatedly resisted those efforts, Axios reported Nov. 11.

By the time Cantor hosted Huang in New York, Lutnick had also received a classified intelligence warning, according to a Nov. 10 Axios report, about Huang's ties to a suspected Chinese spy and had appeared alongside the CEO at a G20 technology summit in North Carolina.

Even as Cantor pared back its Nvidia stake, it continued doing business across the chipmaker's AI empire. A CNBC review of securities filings, corporate announcements and Wall Street research found the firm has helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for Nvidia's business partners while maintaining close ties to the chipmaker's leadership.

Those ties have drawn fresh scrutiny following Huang's resignation Thursday and Axios' reporting that Lutnick repeatedly resisted a crackdown on companies suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, despite President Donald Trump authorizing new export restrictions on those companies for a third time on Nov. 5.

An ethics expert said the relationship between Lutnick and his former firm's investments may raise questions, given what the secretary knew about Nvidia.

Richard Painter, the former chief White House ethics lawyer for President George W. Bush and now a corporate law professor at the University of Minnesota, said that while "there's no proof of" Lutnick sharing nonpublic information with Cantor Fitzgerald, "the appearance doesn't look great."

"His conversations with his sons better be about publicly available information," Painter told CNBC.

There is no evidence that Lutnick's sons had advance knowledge of the intelligence concerns, that changes in Cantor's reported holdings were tied to any warnings or that the firm's business interests influenced their father's decisions.

"Cantor has to date from time to time had only immaterial stand-alone proprietary positions in Nvidia, unlike the positions reflected in 13F filings which were entered into in the ordinary course of business in connection with client swap transactions, that are common in institutional markets," a Cantor spokesperson told CNBC.

Cantor declined to answer CNBC's other questions. The Commerce Department, the White House, Howard Lutnick, Brandon Lutnick and Kyle Lutnick did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment or detailed questions about the findings.

As scrutiny of Huang intensified, Cantor Chairman Brandon Lutnick was publicly praising the chipmaker's leadership. "Nvidia is one of the great companies on the planet, and they have an amazing leadership team," Brandon Lutnick told Fox Business on Wednesday.

Trump is standing by Howard Lutnick. A White House official told Reuters on Thursday that the president maintains "complete confidence" in the commerce secretary.

But cracks in the administration's unity emerged Friday, when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that the departments of Treasury, Defense and State and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative all "were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months."

Bessent pointed to Commerce as the department responsible for imposing the entity list, which identifies restricted businesses and other groups, adding, "You will have to ask them about their internal processes."

Nvidia was Cantor's second-largest reported stock position before Howard Lutnick left Wall Street to become commerce secretary in February 2025, behind only bitcoin investor MicroStrategy, now known as Strategy. At the end of 2024, the firm disclosed more than 3.5 million Nvidia shares worth $479 million, according to its quarterly securities filing.

That share count held steady through September 2025, but its value climbed 36% to $652 million, according to Cantor's quarterly securities filing, as the Trump administration moved over the summer to ease restrictions on Nvidia's H20 chip sales to China.

Over the following six months, however, the number of Nvidia shares Cantor reported holding fell by 49%, to 3 million in December and 1.78 million by the end of March 2026, with their value dropping from $652 million to $310 million, according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings.

Pressure on Howard Lutnick was also mounting on Capitol Hill. Sens. Jim Banks, R-Ind., and Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., in March urged the secretary to suspend or reconsider Nvidia's export licenses after three people linked to Nvidia customer Super Micro Computer were indicted on charges of conspiring to smuggle AI chips to China.

"The Trump administration, I think, leaks like a sieve when it comes to nonpublic government information getting to various hedge fund guys," Painter said, though he stressed there is no evidence Howard Lutnick had shared such information with his sons.

The filings do not establish why Cantor's reported share count fell or whether its overall financial exposure to Nvidia declined. Nvidia’s stock had more than doubled from its April 2025 lows by late October, before retreating in the following months. The stock fell about 6.5% between the end of September and the end of March.

Cantor's reported Nvidia holdings remained near that lower level through June 30, the latest quarter covered by public disclosures, at 1.81 million shares. Its next quarterly filing is due Monday.

Cantor has not publicly explained the decline.

Most of those shares were attributed to CF Secured, a Cantor brokerage subsidiary that uses stocks and derivatives to hedge customer transactions, according to its audited financial statements. Cantor also disclosed substantial Nvidia options positions during the time period CNBC examined, overwhelmingly skewed toward put options, which can protect against declines in the stock price.

As concerns about Huang escalated inside the Trump administration in May, according to the Nov. 11 Axios report, Cantor was helping finance the expansion of one of Nvidia's newest business partners, securities filings show.

On May 7, Nvidia and Australia-based cloud computing provider IREN announced a five-year, $3.4 billion cloud computing contract and a strategic partnership giving the chipmaker the right to invest up to $2.1 billion in IREN.

"That's not a passive financial investment. Nvidia is a partner who wins as we deliver," IREN co-CEO Daniel Roberts told investors on the company's quarterly earnings call that day.

Five days later, as Trump headed to China aboard Air Force One, Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned him about Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, The New York Times reported Tuesday. Huang, who had not initially been invited on the trip, joined the president's delegation during a refueling stop in Alaska.

Howard Lutnick had already been sent a highly classified intelligence memo detailing concerns about Huang's relationship, according to the Nov. 10 Axios report.

On May 12, the day Trump departed for China, IREN announced the pricing of a convertible bond offering that ultimately raised $3 billion when it closed two days later. Cantor was one of seven bookrunners on the deal, alongside JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs.

On the day the offering closed, May 14, Lutnick's Commerce Department quietly cleared roughly 10 Chinese companies, including Alibaba and ByteDance, to buy Nvidia's advanced H200 chips, though some of those approvals predated the intelligence memo.

It is unclear when IREN hired Cantor for the offering or how much the firm earned from the deal. Cantor declined to answer CNBC's questions about its work with IREN.

Cantor reported a substantial position in IREN's stock.

By the end of June, Cantor reported $115 million in IREN shares and $362 million in Nvidia shares. Together, the two companies accounted for more than 9% of the value of Cantor's reported $5.2 billion in securities holdings, excluding options, according to CNBC's analysis of the filing.

IREN was not the only company in Nvidia's orbit that turned to Cantor for financing.

In October 2025, Cantor advised AI infrastructure developer Lancium on a $600 million financing deal to support its data center campus in Abilene, Texas, the first site of Stargate, the massive AI infrastructure project backed by OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle.

Newmark, a commercial real estate firm controlled by Cantor, also helped finance the Abilene campus, arranging a $7.1 billion construction loan in May 2025.

Ten months later, Nvidia agreed to invest $2 billion for a roughly 20% stake in Lancium, with up to $1 billion more tied to future milestones, The Information reported in August. Lancium, which is also backed by Blackstone, confirmed an investment and a technology partnership on Aug. 24 without disclosing financial terms.

It's unclear whether Cantor continued advising Lancium after the financing deal or played a role in Nvidia's investment. Neither Cantor nor Lancium responded to questions about the investment.

Cantor's reported ties also extend to Nvidia's supply chain.

TSMC received billions of dollars in federal subsidies created during the Biden administration and administered by the Commerce Department to fund its U.S. manufacturing expansion.

Democratic senators called for an ethics investigation in December into whether the Lutnick family stood to benefit from Howard Lutnick's push to expand AI data centers.

And on Wednesday, Sens. Warren and Chris Coons, D-Del., demanded that Howard Lutnick, Rubio and White House chief of staff Stephen Miller preserve records on Nvidia's chip exports to China and intelligence warnings about Huang.

The senators questioned whether "prudent defensive counter-intelligence action was taken or national security recommendations were overruled."

"The place where I think the Trump administration has most failed here is in being persuaded by Jensen Huang and others to license the export of some advanced chips," Coons said Friday on CNBC's "Squawk Box," accusing the administration of turning a blind eye to the black market for more advanced chips.

MEMPHIS, Tenn. — Day'Ron Sharpe is making the jump from backup bruiser to full-time starter and complete player.

And so far, the transition has been going well.

That's the fourth-best rating in the entire league among all qualified centers.

Brooklyn Nets center Day'ron Sharpe (20) shoots a layup against the Charlotte Hornets on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST

#2736. How Rockstar's 'GTA VI' release could reshape gaming, streaming and even paid time off

It's been 13 years since the last installment of Grand Theft Auto, and fans are getting ready for what analysts say could be the biggest video game launch of all time.

The latest game in the franchise, "Grand Theft Auto VI," is set to launch on Nov. 19, after Take-Two Interactive's Rockstar Games delayed its launch twice. Roth analyst Eric Handler estimated the game maker spent more than $1 billion developing the game.

Sales figures could end up breaking records. Sensor Tower estimated over 12 million preorders through Nov. 13, and Morgan Stanley forecast the game could sell 40 million copies by March 2027.

Beyond launch week, the Grand Theft Auto, or GTA, franchise has a track record of lasting engagement over many years. Even 13 years after launch, "Grand Theft Auto V" is one of the top five most viewed games on Twitch this year.

In anticipation of the game's launch, investors have been taking note: Take-two's stock has more than doubled since the beginning of 2023.

The release is seen as not only a monumental moment for developer Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two, but also a massive opportunity for the entire gaming industry.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick addressed demand in a recent "Squawk Box" interview, saying, "We tend to be pretty judicious when we talk about this sort of thing, but our expectations were high and they are being vastly exceeded so far."

A creator who goes by the name Deansocool, who has 375,000 followers on Twitch and posts content to YouTube and other social platforms as well, said "GTA VI" will enable creators to grow their audience and provide a massive opportunity for newer streamers to make a name for themselves.

"This game is going to make a lot of millionaires in 2027. A lot of creators gotta understand this is it. This is that golden ticket. This is like a hundred times bigger than Fortnite," he said in an interview with CNBC.

"It goes beyond this launch moment into this sustaining opportunity for them to grow, build, engage and retain their audience and ultimately support themselves by making money," said Twitch Chief Product Officer Mike Minton.

The release of the latest Grand Theft Auto title could draw so much attention that its impact will be felt beyond just the world of gaming.

BambooHR, a workplace time-off platform, reported that paid time off requests for the "GTA VI" release date are nearly 13% higher than equivalent days in 2024 and 2025. It also noted that nearly one in five workers are planning to take time off for the launch.

PwC issued a report examining all the different sectors of the economy that could benefit from the game's launch — or be hurt by it. The firm projected that food delivery companies could see a surge from hunkered-down gamers, and Miami tourism could benefit. PwC noted that foreign visitors to Seoul's Bukchon Hanok Village, which inspired a location in the hit Netflix movie KPop Demon Hunters, increased 118% in the four weeks following the movie's debut.

Music streaming also looks set to get a boost. Tom Petty's "Love Is a Long Road," which appeared in the first "GTA VI" trailer in December 2023, reportedly saw Spotify streams jump by more than 37,000%.

On the downside, the game could distract from movies and streaming entertainment.

"How are people spending Thanksgiving? There's a lot of sports on TV, but you've also got a pretty solid group of your demographics that are going to be focused on playing 'GTA VI,'" said Bart Spiegel, who leads PwC's Global Entertainment & Media sector. "You're going to start to pull eyeballs away from video streaming platforms.

"I think you're going to hear a lot of analyst calls in the first quarter of 2027 saying, 'Hey, listen, some of our numbers were down because of the release of this game,'" Spiegel added.

Rockstar Games declined CNBC's interview request. Watch the video above to learn more.

#2735. 'No racism in Spain' – De la Fuente message for Tuchel

Luis de la Fuente has dismissed concerns over racism in Spanish football before the national team's Uefa Nations League meeting with England in Madrid on Sunday.

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel had earlier confirmed he would remind his players of Uefa's anti-racism protocol before the fixture, which will determine who finishes top of League A Group 3.

While he has stressed he didn't expect there to be any incidents, the visit will be England's first to the Spanish capital since a notorious 2004 encounter at the Bernabeu was overshadowed by racist chanting directed at their players.

Spain head coach De la Fuente was asked whether Tuchel's message to his players showed there was still work needed to tackle racism in Spain.

But he responded: "What I'd tell you, and you can tell Thomas, is that in Spain, there's no racism.

"Just like that, crystal clear. Just like in England, there's no racism in Spain. We aren't racist, any of us."

The Spanish Football Federation was fined last month and ordered to partially close a stadium after supporters directed Islamophobic and xenophobic chants towards Muslims during a match against Egypt in Barcelona.

In the domestic game, Real Madrid's Brazilian forward Vinicius Jr has been a vocal anti-racism campaigner after frequently being on the end of racist chanting - and worse. In 2024 three Valencia fans were sentenced to eight months in prison for abusing him at a match.

Uefa operates a three-step protocol, allowing referees to stop matches, take players off the pitch temporarily and, ultimately, abandon a game if discriminatory behaviour continues.

Tuchel said on Friday: "Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid]. And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch."

However, when asked again about his views at a pre-match news conference on Saturday, Tuchel added: "I never talk about racism in Spain.

"I answered politely a question about what happens, I never expect racism. I got asked, 'what will happen if and if and if?'. And I said, 'if it happens, there's a protocol in place'. That's it.

"But my trust is that we have a friendly atmosphere, that we have an atmosphere who is clearly in favour of the Spanish team, and that football does what it does best: brings people together and not divide people."

Midfielder Declan Rice said: "In the past, I've experienced that in Montenegro and Bulgaria and there was a protocol in place that we followed - we came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.

"The times we are in now, 2026, there should never be racism in football. It's shocking we still have it in the game today.

"I don't want to think about if one of our players or their players is racially abused because that would be a horrible mark on football."

Focusing on the match itself, De la Fuente believed both teams are currently at the pinnacle of world football, although he rejected the suggestion one could simply replicate the other's playing style.

Spain were crowned World Cup winners in the summer, while England finished third after losing to Argentina in the semi-finals.

"I prefer the Spanish model. It's very recognisable, the players are perfectly adapted," said De la Fuente. "The English model is very good, but you have to have that type of player. Neither England can play like Spain, nor Spain like England."

He suggested Spain had faced increasingly aggressive opposition as their recent success had raised expectations.

"It's our best moment in a long time," added De la Fuente, whose side also lifted the Euro 2024 title by beating England. "They are all much more aggressive to beat us now than in other times."

He also defended the value of Spanish players, arguing their performances often outweighed their transfer-market prices compared with those in the Premier League.

"Spanish footballers surprise me that, compared to what is paid in England, they are very cheap," he explained. "I see them as better, in my opinion. Everyone in their market can set the prices."

On the fitness of forward Lamine Yamal, he remained cautious over whether the Barcelona teenager would start or how long he could manage.

"We will see if he is a starter, but if he comes out, it's because he's fit to play," said De la Fuente.

#2734. How does Seattle Seahawks’ offense look with Drew Lock at quarterback for Week 10 matchup against Las Vegas Raiders?

Week 10 features an old-school AFC West rivalry as the then-Oakland, now Las Vegas Raiders and Seattle Seahawks had plenty of noteworthy divisional battles in the '80s and '90s before the NFL's realignment that pushed Seattle into the NFC. To preview this weekend's matchup, Silver and Black Pride reached out to our friends at Field Gulls, and John Gilbert was kind enough to answer a few questions about the Seahawks for Raider Nation.

Q: Sam Darnold has already been ruled out, meaning Drew Lock will make his fourth appearance and third start this season. What's the difference in the Seahawks' offense with Lock at quarterback, and what's the fanbase's confidence level in him as the starter?

A: In years past, the answer to this would hark back to Pete Carroll's 2023 comments about Lock making a couple of boneheaded throws. But when Lock has played this season, he has done a phenomenal job protecting the football.

Darnold has missed two full games and only played five snaps in the season opener against the New England Patriots. Yet in spite of that, he is tied with Matthew Stafford for the most interceptions thrown in the NFC.

On the flip side, Lock has five touchdowns and no interceptions while starting twice and playing most of the game against the Patriots. Of course, both of Lock's starts came against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Arizona defense has done a solid job helping opposing quarterbacks bolster their stat lines this season, so we'll see what Lock can do against the Raiders.

Q: Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off a season where he led the NFL with nearly 1,800 receiving yards and won Offensive Player of the Year. So far in 2026, he's the first and currently only player to eclipse the 1,000-yard mark while averaging about 10 yards per game more than he did last year. What makes JSN such a tough cover? Any suggestions for how to keep him in check?

A: JSN has simply become a monster. He's a very smooth and fluid route runner, and at the foundation of his greatness is the simple fact that all of his route stems look the same, making it impossible for defensive backs to anticipate what is coming.

Add in great hands, a phenomenal work ethic and the reality that he is far and away the most dangerous offensive weapon in the Seattle arsenal. It's a recipe to continue to feed him the ball until defenses can find a way to slow him down.

Teams have tried almost everything to slow JSN down, but a consistent weakness has not yet been found. Jamming him at the line doesn't stop him. Bracketing doesn't stop him. Whatever opponents do, he just continues to find ways to get open and keep the offense moving.

Q: Seattle's rushing attack ranks 18th in yards per game, 25th in yards per carry and 27th in EPA per rush, according to Sumer Sports. Are the issues as simple as the offense missing Klint Kubiak and Kenneth Walker III? Has adding Quenton Nelson helped at all?

A: Losing Kenneth Walker III to the Chiefs in free agency certainly hurt. The two biggest things the Seattle run game has missed for most of the first half of the season were the explosiveness and the ball security that Walker brought to the table.

Yes, he had a style that could be infuriating at times, as he had a tendency to try to bounce so many runs outside looking for the big play. But the simple fact is that he has the burst and speed to create an outsized number of explosive plays, even while consistently finishing in the bottom half of the league in success rate.

During his four seasons in Seattle, Walker fumbled a total of three times on 821 regular-season rushing attempts, while his replacements (Jadarian Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani) have put the ball on the ground six times in 195 rushing attempts so far this season.

With that said, Zach Charbonnet is back in the lineup after tearing his ACL in the 2025 postseason, and his presence has been an instant upgrade at the position. Charbonnet is never going to present the big-play threat that Walker brought to the field on every rushing attempt, but Charbonnet is a disciplined back who will follow his blocking, while providing solid pass protection from the backfield in passing situations.

As for Quenton Nelson, so far the trade has produced more excitement and hype than on-field production. Nelson apparently suffered a minor knee injury before the trade and had a procedure to address the issue. As such, with the Seahawks enjoying a bye week after facing off against the Raiders, he likely won't be back in action again until Week 12 against the San Francisco 49ers.

Q: Imagine you're Kubiak game-planning for Fernando Mendoza's first start against the vaunted Seahawks' defense. How would you attack the defense and give the rookie quarterback his best chance at having success? Keep in mind that the Raiders are one of the few teams that are worse at running the ball than the Seahawks are.

A: Where Kubiak really seemed to excel in Seattle was creating tendencies, or the appearance of tendencies, and then in high-leverage situations making it look like the offense is following that tendency, only to break off for a big play.

So, whatever tendencies the Raiders offense has put on tape through the first half of the season, I expect those tendencies to be thrown out the window at key times within the games as Kubiak looks for big plays.

The reality is that while the Seahawks defense is great, so far in 2026 the Seahawks offense hasn't shown to be on par with the 2025 group, and between conservative playcalling and Drew Lock battling oblique and elbow issues, it might only take a couple of big plays for the Raiders to play spoilers against the defending champs.

Q: Between Leonard Williams, Byron Murphy II, Devon Witherspoon, Ernest Jones IV and Nick Emmanwori, Seattle's defense is filled with studs. If you had to pick one to deem the biggest key or X-factor for the unit, who would it be and why?

A: As cliché as it sounds, there is no one piece that makes the defense tick. What makes Mike Macdonald's defenses so good is that all eleven players are on the same page, doing their jobs at a high level. All of the big names on defense play key roles, but as a whole the group has enough depth that a single missing piece doesn't send things off the rails.

With that all said, everything starts in the trenches. So if Williams and Murphy aren't able to do their thing up front, it leaves the rest of the defense hanging.

#2733. Everton Face Forest Fight For Brazilian Defender: Is £12.5m Worth It?

Everton and Nottingham Forest are both monitoring Grêmio centre-back Gustavo Martins ahead of January, according to Sport Witness, which cites German outlet Fussball.eu. The 24-year-old Brazilian wants to play in Europe, but Grêmio aren't selling cheaply.

They reportedly want £10-12.5m, almost double the £5.8m Shakhtar Donetsk were ready to pay before a minor thigh injury derailed that deal in the previous window. Grêmio also want a new three-year contract, because his current one expires in December 2027, and a renewal would strengthen their hand against English suitors.

Martins is 6ft 3in, is right-footed and has started 13 of his 15 appearances this year, covering 1,208 minutes. He has won 67.3% of his aerial duels, made 65 clearances and completed 90.9% of his passes, although his average FotMob rating is a modest 6.91.

FotMob also lists right-back as a second position. The drawbacks are just as visible, with no goals, earlier knee and thigh injuries, and a listed weight of only 68-70kg that Premier League strikers will test.

Everton sit fifth after a third straight win, 3-1 against Coventry on 6 November, yet the defence looked shaky. Jarrad Branthwaite was poor for Coventry's goal and picked up a yellow card, while 33-year-old James Tarkowski was involved in a first-half penalty appeal. It was a contrast with the start of the season, when David Moyes's side kept five clean sheets in their first seven games.

RIO DE JANEIRO, BRAZIL – APRIL 14: Gustavo Martins of Gremio celebrates after scoring the first goal of his team during the match between Vasco da Gama and Gremio as part of Brasileirao 2024 at Sao Januario Stadium on April 14, 2024 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. (Photo by Wagner Meier/Getty Images)

Everton should keep the interest alive but refuse to pay Grêmio's full price. Tarkowski is 33, and Moyes leans on him heavily, while Branthwaite's injury record means the club needs a second centre-back it trusts week to week. Martins offers that profile, being tall, strong in the air, comfortable on the ball and proven over 1,208 minutes of regular football.

The money is the problem. FotMob values him at roughly £1.7m, and Shakhtar's £5.8m is the only real market benchmark, so £12.5m for a defender who has never played outside Brazil asks Everton to pay for potential. A January arrival would also need to handle Premier League physicality mid-season, which is a bigger test for a slim 24-year-old than the numbers suggest.

The sensible approach is an offer close to Shakhtar's figure. If Grêmio extend him to 2030, Everton should walk away. If they don't, he enters next summer with six months left on his deal, and the buyer holds the leverage.

#2732. SpaceX catches upper stage of Starship rocket in historic first

After a booster explosion on Friday, SpaceX successfully caught the upper stage, or spacecraft, portion of its massive Starship rocket from orbit on Saturday — a triumphant milestone for the company.

SpaceX made the historic catch using its "chopsticks," mechanical arms attached to a launch tower, at its facility in Starbase, Texas.

Test Flight 15, the most ambitious Starship test yet, marked the first time Musk's company attempted to catch both the rocket's booster and upper stage.

During the first phase of the test flight on Friday, SpaceX failed to catch and recover the booster, instead diverting it to an offshore splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico where it exploded before hitting the water.

The rocket's upper stage then continued into orbit and flew around the Earth 14 times before successfully landing on SpaceX's launch tower, nicknamed Mechazilla.

The Hawaii Department of Transportation issued a temporary pause on some West Coast flights Friday, due to debris risk from the flight. Separately, the FAA issued a rare, nationwide ground stop due to telecommunications system failures. (Both of those orders have since been lifted.)

Making Starship a reliable and fully reusable rocket is critical to SpaceX's ambitions. In the near term, the company needs Starship to send more satellites into orbit to expand its Starlink satellite internet service, which is currently the company's profit center.

SpaceX is also expected to use Starship to bring astronauts and cargo from lunar orbit to the Moon's surface and back for NASA. Musk also has a grand vision to use Starship to "colonize Mars" and "make humanity multi-planetary."

During Test Flight 15 on Friday, SpaceX released another 26 of its newest Starlink v3 satellites into orbit, growing its commercial satellite internet network.

The company's constellation already included over 11,000 satellites in low Earth orbit. One Starship rocket can carry up to 60 Starlink v3 satellites, the company has said.

#2730. Warriors get demolished by Stephon Castle, Spurs

Friday was always going to be an incredibly difficult game for the Golden State Warriors. They were on the road, taking on a San Antonio Spurs team that had won 10 consecutive games. Just on strength of opponent, it was the hardest game of the year for the Dubs.

And then "hard" turned into "impossible" when Steph Curry was injured during Wednesday's loss to the Houston Rockets. With Curry sidelined, the Warriors were, essentially, without hope in this game.

Still, about once a year the Warriors — like most teams — are good for a shocking upset bid when undermanned. Could this be the night where they're competitive against all odds?

It only took a few possessions for the answer to be an emphatic "no." Steve Kerr opted for a small starting lineup — De'Anthony Melton, Brandin Podziemski, Will Richard, Yaxel Lendeborg, and Draymond Green — hoping to outrun a team that they would be catastrophically undersized against, regardless of who they started.

And boy howdy, that — like everything the team tried — did not work. The opening possessions went exactly the way you would expect: the Warriors could not find an inch of space, while the Spurs broke them down. It felt like a team of seven-footers was playing a team of five-footers … it seemed like every Warriors pass was deflected, and every shot was blocked or contested. In the time it took you to figure out how to get this Prime Video game on your TV, San Antonio had taken a 7-0 lead.

They were getting everything they wanted on offense, using the gravity and playmaking of Victor Wembanyama to fully break down a helpless Warriors defense. Kerr called his first timeout less than three minutes into the game, with the Spurs leading 12-0. That timeout helped Golden State's defense a tiny bit, but it did nothing for their offense. 12-0 became 14-0 became 16-0 became 18-0, the best start to a game in San Antonio's history.

Finally, more than halfway through the quarter, the Warriors — who started the game 0-for-11 from the field — got on the board, when Gui Santos absorbed some contact for a tough and-one.

But even that play was emblematic of the struggles, as Santos missed the free throw, and just a few seconds later, the Spurs converted it into a three.

Santos' bucket did not break any dam. Offense was still borderline impossible for the Dubs to come by, though they finally found a few buckets when Wembanyama took a rest. San Antonio's offense, on the other hand, didn't change at all with their superstar sidelined, as Stephon Castle took it upon him to thoroughly feast on Warriors defenders. That, combined with the Spurs making it rain from deep, led to a 38-14 San Antonio advantage after the first quarter. With no Curry, it was clear that the game was already over.

Golden State played much better defense in the second quarter, and the Spurs' offense got a little discombobulated. But that did nothing for the Warriors' offense, which was still stuck on life support. Every bucket was hard to come by — though LJ Cryer had some nice bursts to give fans something to cheer for — and Golden State could do nothing to cut into the deficit. A bad foul on a De'Aaron Fox three with less than a second remaining punctuated an awful half, and the Spurs went to the locker rooms leading 66-33.

The Warriors opened the third quarter with a pair of threes, and then, for all intents and purposes, they walked off the court and called it a night. San Antonio was taller, longer, stronger, more athletic, faster, and happy to flex all of those advantages in every area of the game. The second half was window dressing, and the Spurs weren't even incentivized to take their foot off the gas, since it was an NBA Cup game, and thus, point differential mattered. The lead ballooned to 43 points for the Spurs, before coming back to an ever-so-slightly less-disrespectful 38 by the final buzzer, with San Antonio winning 123-85.

Cryer was the Warriors' lone bright spot, as he scored a career-high 20 points with six assists (and no turnovers!), while shooting 6-for-11 from three-point range. Charles Bassey, who had 11 points and five rebounds, was the only other Golden State player in double figures.

With Curry out, the Dubs are going to rely on Lendeborg and Podziemski to carry the offense, but neither could do so against the ranginess of San Antonio's excellent defense. Lendeborg had far and away the worst game of his young career, as he shot 1-for-13 from the field for three points, seven rebounds, one assist, and three turnovers. Podz wasn't much better, as he had eight points on 2-for-10 shooting. As a team, the Warriors shot a paltry 33.3% (31-for-93) from the field. The Spurs' length gave the Dubs fits, as they shot significantly worse inside the arc than beyond it … they shot 15-for-41 (36.6%) on threes, but just 16-for-52 (30.8%) on twos, while only earning 11 free throws.

Castle led San Antonio with a brilliant game, finishing with 32 points, five rebounds, and six assists. Wembanyama only played 21 minutes, but that was enough for him to have 12 points, 12 rebounds, six assists, one steal, and two blocks.

The Dubs now get the weekend off, before facing the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday.

#2729. Nvidia board urged to consider 'potential return of Jensen Huang' by two major investors

Two major Nvidia shareholders are calling on the board of directors to weigh all options for the company's future leadership, including "the potential return of Jensen Huang."

Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner posted a letter on X on Friday that urges Nvidia's board to "pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia." The letter is also signed by Atreides Management's Gavin Baker.

Nvidia was Altimeter Capital's largest disclosed equity holding in its most recent SEC filing, with a 9.4 million-share stake worth nearly $1.9 billion as of June 30. Atreides held 1.2 million shares worth nearly $250 million at the end of June.

The letter said Nvidia will be "capably led" by interim CEO Colette Kress, who served as Nvidia's CFO for 13 years before the board announced Thursday that she'd lead the company in Huang's absence.

"But the Founder and long time incredible leader of this extraordinary company has earned the right for a deliberate process that avoids any needless rush to replace him before all the facts are known," the letter concludes. The document did not call for Huang's immediate reinstatement.

Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday amid multiple affair allegations, including one with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, who also worked with Nvidia customer Megaspeed. The Singapore-based company is being investigated by the Justice Department for possibly redirecting some of its supply of Nvidia's restricted artificial intelligence chips to China.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said on X Friday that he signed a petition asking to reinstate Huang. A petition circulating online called "Stand with Jensen" claims to have more than 100,000 signatures, including more than 5,000 current Nvidia employees.

Musk said on X Saturday that without Huang, some "critical deals will be lost."

Another letter sent Friday called on U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick to testify about Megaspeed before the House Intelligence Committee.

Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 about whether the Commerce Department is "properly performing its broader role of preventing China from acquiring advanced AI chips," according to the letter. Huang has also been asked to testify.

The Commerce Department originally launched an investigation into Megaspeed that was moved to the Justice Department in 2025 after Nvidia's lawyer contacted a senior Commerce official, according to The New York Times.

President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit China on Thursday, but doesn't plan to raise Nvidia and the suspected spy affair during his meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping, according to U.S. officials. Musk is expected to join Trump on the trip to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit on Nov. 18 and 19.

#2728. Mirra Andreeva, looking to make history, reaches WTA Finals title match

Mirra Andreeva arrived at Indian Wells last week vying to become just the ninth teenager, and the first in more than 20 years, to win a WTA Finals title.

After Saturday's 6-3, 6-4 win over American Jessica Pegula, the Russian teen is now one step closer to making that history. Andreeva, 19, will face the winner of the Elina Svitolina versus Linda Noskova match on Sunday.

Andreeva saved a break point in the first set, ahead 5-3, to win the game and take the first set.

Then, in the second set, she came from down a break at 3-1 to hold serve and win the five of the final six games to secure the match in front of a capacity crowd inside Stadium 2 at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden.

Indian Wells has been a friendly place for Andreeva. She won the BNP Paribas Open WTA 1000 event here last year, in March 2025.

Andreeva is now just one more win away from joining, Chris Evert (1972), Tracy Austin ('80), Steffi Graf ('87), Gabriela Sabatini ('88), Monica Seles ('90-92), Martina Hingis ('98), Kim Clijsters ('02) and Maria Sharapova ('04) as women who have won a WTA Finals title as a teenager.

#2727. A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession plan, makes it worse.

However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a big haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the company's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

Buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.  Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

This prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

This lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

#2726. Giannis, Bam join LeBron, Wade in exclusive Miami Heat club

The Miami Heat know a thing or two about dynamic duos.

Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo each scored 37 points in a 133-121 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Friday, Nov. 13. Antetokounmpo added nine rebounds and Adebayo notched 14 boards for a double-double in the NBA Cup matchup at the Kaseya Center.

According to the NBA, the two stars join LeBron James and Dwyane Wade as the only other duo in franchise history to score more than 35 points each in the same game.

James and Wade did so twice after James joined Wade on the Heat via "The Decision" in 2010. On March 14, 2012, Wade scored 36 points and James added 35 in a loss to the Chicago Bulls. They also reached the mark on Feb. 26, 2013 when James had 40 points and Wade tossed in 39 in a double-overtime win over the Sacramento Kings. The two won back-to-back championships in 2012 and 2013.

On Friday, Davion Mitchell added 22 points and 17 assists for Miami in the winning effort. Mitchell's 17 assists matched his career high.

Donovan Mitchell led Cleveland with 25 points, seven assists and four rebounds.

This is Antetokounmpo's first season in Miami after a blockbuster trade with the Milwaukee Bucks that included Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr. and Kasparas Jakučionis. The No. 15 overall pick in the 2013 NBA Draft spent his entire career up to this point with the Bucks and decided he wanted a fresh start. He won two league MVPs, was named an All-Star 10 times and won the 2021 NBA Finals in Milwaukee, when he was named Finals MVP.

He will face his former team for the first time on Nov. 18 when the Heat host "A Night in Vice City" to promote the highly-anticipated "Grand Theft Auto 6" video game.

Antetokounmpo is averaging 27.7 points, 12.6 rebounds and 5.2 assists per game this season. Adebayo, who is in his 10th NBA season, all with the Heat, is posting 17.8 points, 8.4 boards, 3.3 assists and a career-high 2.2 steals per outing so far this year. In March, he scored 83 points in a game, the second-most in NBA history.

#2725. Steelers activate DT Derrick Harmon off injured reserve

One of Pittsburgh's best run defenders is back to help bolster an already successful defensive line.

The Steelers announced on Saturday afternoon that defensive tackle Derrick Harmon has been activated off injured reserve. Cornerback Terrell Smith was waived to create room on the 53-man roster.

Harmon is still listed as questionable ahead of the Steelers' Week 10 matchup, but his activation is a good sign for his availability.

Harmon suffered a foot injury in the first half of the Steelers' loss at Cleveland on Thursday, Oct. 1. He was placed on IR and missed the next five weeks (four games).

His last full game was against the Bengals on Sept. 27. In four games, Harmon logged 12 tackles, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one sack.

The 2025 first-round pick is a significant component of Pittsburgh's run defense, a unit that gave up an average of over 80 yards more on the ground last year (five games) when Harmon was out of the lineup.

This season, regardless of whether Harmon has played, the Steelers are a top-five unit. Patrick Graham's defense is allowing 83.9 rushing yards per game, third in the NFL. The Steelers only allowed 100 yards once in his absence.

Harmon returns for arguably the biggest game in the AFC this season as the Steelers face the Bengals on Sunday Night Football. The winner will hold sole possession of first place in the AFC North and the Steelers would own a two-game lead in Cincinnati after sweeping the season series against their rival.

#2724. Saints passing attack has advantage in matchup versus Panthers

Week 10 includes a battle for first place in the NFC South with the New Orleans Saints hosting the Carolina Panthers. The Saints and Panthers are both 3-5, with the winner grabbing sole possession of the division lead. New Orleans has won two of their last three games, while the Panthers are in the midst of a three-game losing streak.

Most of the success that the Saints have had offensively has been because of quarterback Tyler Shough and his receivers. However, New Orleans has gotten off to excruciatingly bad starts in every game this year. They'll be facing a Carolina defense that ranks 21st overall but has fared better statistically against the pass. It's there that we focus this analysis of Sunday's clash.

▪︎ 211.5 yards per game (9th)▪︎ 63.3% completion percentage▪︎ 12 touchdowns (16th)▪︎ 5 interceptions (20th)▪︎ 11 sacks▪︎ 32 QB hits

If not for 406 passing yards given up to Detroit in Week 4, the Panthers would rank even higher against the pass. Four of Carolina's other seven opponents have been held to less than 200 net yards through the air. However, the Packers and Broncos have both put up over 220 passing yards against the Panthers in the last two weeks. This can be mostly attributed to mounting injuries in the team's secondary.

Carolina has been without starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson for five games each, greatly thinning their coverage unit. The good news for the Panthers is that Jackson (groin) was a full participant in practice by the end of this week and could be activated off injured reserve to play against the Saints. Rookie fourth-round choice Will Lee (knee) also was back at practice in full capacity and likely resumes his starting duties. Lee's 7 pass breakups lead the Panthers, but practice squad player Corey Thornton is the only Panthers corner to have an interception. Undersized Chau Smith-Wade and rookie Malcolm DeWalt IV round out the team's current corner crew.

Carolina does have two physical safeties in Tre'von Moehrig and Nick Scott with two solid backups in Lathan Ransom and Zakee Wheatley. Scott, the usual free safety, has by far the most range. Wheatley has probably the best ball skills of the four and has an interception with four passes broken up. At linebacker, Devin Lloyd and Brian Okereke are not only Carolina's leading tacklers but also strong in coverage. The athletic Lloyd has a team-high two interceptions, returning one for a touchdown, with him and Okereke (one interception) combining to break up nine opposing throws, but Okereke (foot) will be sidelined against the Saints.

Carolina was one of the league's worst at pressuring the quarterback last year. Despite a handful of new additions, the same trend has continued this season. Edge Princely Umanmielen, a 2025 third-round pick, leads the Panthers with just 3 sacks. Pricey free-agent acquisition Jaelan Phillips has contributed 2.5 sacks and a team-best 6 QB hits. Both are capable of much more disruption, which the Panthers are counting on for their stretch run. Carolina is also capable of disruption on the inside, but hasn't gotten it from Derrick Brown, Lee Hunter, Tershawn Wharton, or Bobby Brown III. The Panthers' down linemen have yet to record a sack this season, with the group combining for just six QB hits.

▪︎ 230.5 yards per game (14th)▪︎ 66.2% completion percentage▪︎ 14 touchdowns (12th)▪︎ 6 interceptions (16th)▪︎ 20 sacks

Second-year quarterback Tyler Shough has been under tremendous pressure all year thanks to a porous offensive line and the absence of a competent running game. Despite this, Shough has been productive on a fairly consistent basis and particularly clutch in critical situations. Dealing with an injured non-throwing hand, Shough has shown both poise and accuracy from the pocket and the ability to escape the rush to make plays with his legs or deliver with pinpoint precision on the move.

Shough's favorite target is wideout Chris Olave, who is well on his way to the best numbers of his five-year career. Olave has caught 56 of his 83 targets for 734 yards and two touchdowns. Those impressive numbers are only part of the story. Olave's route precision and ability to quickly diagnose coverages allow consistent production in spite of heavy defensive attention.

Wideout Devaughn Vele has been a terrific complement to Olave, particularly on third downs or key situations. Vele has 35 receptions for 365 yards and three scores, with 19 of his catches resulting in a first down. Shough's trust in Vele is clear, with the receiver often converting with acrobatic catches in traffic. Tight end Juwan Johnson is another security blanket for Shough. Though he's cooled after a hot start, Johnson has 28 catches for 289 yards and a team-best four touchdowns while providing a huge matchup problem for most defenses.

New Orleans has young depth at wideout. Rookies Barion Brown and Bryce Lance have been involved and have flashed some playmaking skills, but not on a consistent enough basis. Rookie first-round pick Jordyn Tyson got his first NFL action against the Browns last week. Tyson immediately showed why he was a top-10 pick with impressive routes and athleticism. Look for him to be a bigger part of the offense with each week.

Alvin Kamara has not been productive as a runner, but still has lethal value as a pass catcher. The return of Travis Etienne (hamstring) from injured reserve will not only boost the running game, but also give Shough another legitimate receiving weapon out of the backfield. The Saints also have two good pass catchers at tight end to back up Johnson with Noah Fant and rookie Oscar Delp. Neither has been a big contributor as a pass catcher, combining for 16 catches and 116 yards. However, both have been used as extra pass protectors recently (as have the running backs) and each is a capable receiver at all three levels.

New Orleans pass protection got a huge boost with the return of left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. from injured reserve last week. Banks and left guard David Edwards make a formidable duo on that side, but there are major questions about the middle and right side of the Saints line. Center Erik McCoy also sustained a biceps injury in that same game and will be sidelined for a minimum of a few weeks. At least initially, right guard Cesar Ruiz will slide into McCoy's spot at center, with either William Sherman or rookie Jeremiah Wright stepping in at guard. Right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) will also be sidelined against Carolina, with his spot taken by either Asim Richards or rookie Mason Murphy. This is typically the spot where Derrick Brown lines up, so certainly an area of concern for New Orleans on Sunday.

Tyler Shough notched his first career victory against Carolina by throwing for 282 yards and two scores in a 2025 Week 10 matchup. Five weeks later, Shough tossed for 272 yards and a touchdown to complete the season sweep. In those two meetings, Shough has completed 72.9% of his throws for 554 yards and three touchdowns without an interception. Chris Olave has also forged All-Pro numbers against the Panthers. In eight career games against Carolina, Olave has 38 receptions for 534 yards and four scores with two 100-yard games and two more outings of over 80 yards.

#2723. Nationwide ground stop followed contractor upgrade to L3Harris telecommunication system: DOT’s Duffy

The longest halt in flight departures to U.S. airports since 9/11 came after updates to a telecommunications system made by L3Harris Technologies, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Saturday, as travel disruptions lingered for thousands of passengers nationwide.

There was "zero evidence" that the problem was caused by something "nefarious" or anything related to artificial intelligence, Bryan Bedford, the head of the Federal Aviation Administration, said at a press conference.

The updates were part of ongoing work of switching from a copper wire system to fiberoptic cable, Duffy said. When a router was switched to fiberoptic cable from copper, it had "flooded" other routers in the air traffic control system with over 1,000 connection attempts roughly every five seconds, Duffy said, creating problems with airplane communications and radar feeds.

Bedford said no FAA facilities went dark but that officials decided to ground flights because of "instability" in information feeds to air traffic control centers that handle en route aircraft at high altitudes and eventually to others closer to airports.

"We were unwilling to take any risk that this propagation could actually result in a center losing connectivity with aircraft," said Bedford.

L3Harris didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

Duffy told the press conference that the FAA is investigating.

"What we're working to determine was whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error, installator error from L3 Harris, or did they install a faulty router," he said.

Flight disruptions continued on Saturday. More than 3,700 U.S. flights were canceled Saturday and close to 2,000 were delayed as of 9:40 a.m. ET, according to flight-tracking site FlightAware. That's on top of about 9,000 U.S. flight cancellations and more than 7,000 delays on Friday, though some disruptions were due to bad weather.

Part of untangling from the ground stop includes getting aircraft where they need to be. The ground stop forced many planes to divert to other airports.

Airlines run one of the lightest schedules on Saturday and are deploying as many spare planes and crews as possible to get travelers and employees where they need to be as they're eager to start fresh for the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday period.

American Airlines, for example, is offering flight attendants extra pay to pick up trips, according to a person familiar with the airline's plans.

Delta Air Lines was offering crews double pay to pick up trips and gave them confirmed seats on flights to get them into position, according to internal company messages seen by CNBC. United Airlines was also offering pilots and flight attendants extra pay to pick up flights through Sunday, according to people familiar with the matter.

American and other airlines said they would change customers' tickets at no fee or fare difference if the outage affected their plans.

Around 3 million people were scheduled to fly on Saturday, according to aviation data firm Cirium.

The FAA had halted departing U.S. flights around 4 p.m. ET on Friday, a ground stop that lasted more than four hours, the longest such pause on departing flights in 25 years.

Duffy on Friday blamed outdated U.S. infrastructure for the problem and said Congress needs to approve more money to overhaul the country's air traffic control. Aging equipment and a shortage of air traffic controllers have angered airline executives for years, who have complained about the cost of resulting disruptions.

It was the second time the FAA has issued a nationwide ground stop since the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks. Trump administration officials have repeatedly said it did not appear to be a cyberattack.

The U.S. has the world's busiest airspace.

"Before clearing flights to resume, we thoroughly tested our systems to confirm they were stable and that operations remain reliable," the FAA said late Friday.

The disruption also upended travel for NBA, NHL and college teams, which struggled to reach their destinations in time for games this weekend.

Duffy said college football teams traveling on charter flights could receive priority.

"I would encourage those football teams to reach out to the FAA to schedule their flight times and make sure they have games going off tomorrow," he said during a Friday press briefing.

The Southeastern Conference announced on X that some games had been moved to Sunday due to the flight disruption.

"We are in close communication with our member institutions to assess potential disruptions and coordinate appropriate responses," the SEC said in a statement shared on X.

The National Football League said that it is putting in three backup referees for three games on Sunday because of the ground stop, "reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns."

— CNBC's April Roach and Jessica Golden contributed to this article.

#2722. Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

(This is the Warren Buffett Watch newsletter, news and analysis on all things Warren Buffett and Berkshire Hathaway. You can sign up here to receive it every Friday evening in your inbox.)

Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

The much more widely held B shares closed at new highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the company's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the company as "banks, insurance, and finance."

The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

Barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks new CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to quickly disclose any sales.

Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

The case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

In the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

All those numbers exclude the company's buybacks of its own stock.

In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway says it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most important ideas.

WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

Two of the — well, all of the important ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

And the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that says it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds."
