The NFL's system to decide who gets compensatory draft picks is complicated, and that's an understatement.

As it stands right now, the Cincinnati Bengals will receive an extra third-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft due to the free agency loss of Trey Hendrickson to the Ravens. And that's one of the reasons the Bengals ended up backing out of their trade with the Eagles for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie on Tuesday before the deadline came at 4 PM.

The Bengals, a little before noon, agreed to send a sixth-round pick to the Eagles in exchange for Ebiketie, but after OverTheCap.com's Nick Korte pointed that the Bengals could lose their compensatory pick in the trade went through, the Bengals backed out.

The Seattle Seahawks signed former Bengals guard Cordell Volson to their practice squad. If he were to make the active roster and play enough snaps as a starter for the Seahawks, he could, potentially, count as a compensatory free agent, which could give the Bengals an extra seventh-round pick and have allowed that Ebiketie trade to go through without sacrificing the third-round compensatory pick.

Again, this is a big "what if" scenario, and I can't even pretend I know the ins and outs of the compensatory system (there are few that do… especially inside the offices of Paycor Stadium), but wouldn't it just seem to work out that way for the Bengals?

#2720. Utah Jazz vs. Houston Rockets: Recap and Final Score

Nov 13, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Utah Jazz guard Darryn Peterson (22) handles the ball against Houston Rockets center Alperen Sengun (28) during the first quarter at Toyota Center. Mandatory Credit: Erik Williams-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

The Utah Jazz fall to the Houston Rockets 125-118 for their twelfth loss of the season, and second NBA Cup game loss.

The Jazz got off to a solid start in the first quarter with respectable defense and ball movement. Although no one could stop Alpren Sengun, who was getting everything he wanted all night long (including every foul call), Jaxon Hayes and Mo Bamba punished his poor drop coverage on the other end by catching lobs.

After the first quarter, the game was tied up at 27 a piece. Jaxon Hayes came out of the game with an injury (the Jazz can't catch a break with the frontcourt injuries!). Like every other game this season, the bench came in and immediately started turning the ball over and giving up easy baskets, putting the Jazz in a 10-point deficit going into the second half.

Then it got exciting. Darryn Peterson and Keyonte George took over the game, attacking the rim, spraying out the 3-point shooters, and getting stops on the other end. Ace Bailey was hitting his 3s, Keyonte had an amazing 4-point play, and Darryn was controling the game and getting any shot he wanted. Before long, the 10-point deficit became a 10-point lead. Utah's offense was looking as good as it had all season. Darryn Peterson scored 12 points in the first 6 minutes of the third quarter.

But apparently Will Hardy wanted to change things. Enter: Isaiah Collier and Brice Sensabaugh. Instead of going with what was clearly working, Isaiah Collier pounded the air out of the ball as the lead was erased almost as quickly as it was built.

It was about to get ugly again, but Keyonte George came alive, scoring 23 points in the second half. He was aggressive, attacking the basket and creating contact, but the refs decided only the Rockets were allowed to shoot free throws this game.

Bamba wasn't doing anything to stop Sengun, who scored pretty much every time he touched the basketball within 15 feet of the rim. Tony Bradley also played 12 minutes, but didn't do much to stop him either.

However, despite the bench, the refs, and Sengun, the Jazz were still in it. After a beautiful jumper at the elbow from Peterson, the Jazz were down one with 2:40 to go. Amen Thompson scored to put Houston up three, and Keyonte had a terrible turnover, trying to dump the ball down to Bamba. After George's turnover, Sensabaugh bricked an offbalance lay, and Sengun scored on the other end.

With 11 seconds left in the game, the Jazz were down 5. Any reasonable person would have assumed a play would be drawn up for Darryn to score. But no. Not only did that not happen, but he was benched for none of than Svi Mykhailiuk.

Sensabaugh got the ball and did nothing other than jump out of bounds and try to get a foul call.

Another heartbreaking loss in a very winnable game. The bench is horrendous and Will Hardy continues to make mind boggling decisions with the game on the line. Why did we tank all year for Peterson if we are just going to play Brice and Svi at the end of games!?!?

The young core of the Jazz played great, but it wasn't enough. Keyonte, Ace, and Darryn have very bright futures.

Alpren Sengun had 43 points and 12 rebounds.

Kevin Durant did what he does, scoring 22 points without hardly breaking a sweat.

Darryn Peterson finished with 28 points and 7 rebounds for his fifth straight 20-point game. This season has been rough, but at least we have Darryn Peterson.

#2718. Juice your growth and save on taxes in this workplace investment account

Workers are in the heart of open enrollment season for next year's benefits, and rising healthcare costs are shining a spotlight on an offering that includes a tax-advantaged investment account.

Healthcare expenses are climbing for workers and employers alike, with average total family premiums, including the employer's share, averaging $28,303, up 5% from a year ago, according to data from health policy organization KFF, formerly the Kaiser Family Foundation.

To manage the costs, a growing number of employers are moving to high-deductible health plans, which work alongside health savings accounts or HSAs. Almost 40% of companies with at least 10 employees that offer health benefits also have an HSA-qualified plan, KFF found.

Health savings accounts have three major tax advantages. First, contributions that your employer automatically deducts from your pay aren't taxed. Second, money stashed into the HSA grows free of taxes. Finally, you can make tax-free withdrawals for qualified health expenses – just be sure to save your receipts.

"I love HSAs because of their triple-tax advantage," said Eileen Olson, CFP and founder of Emerald Wealth in Daufuskie Island, South Carolina, near Savannah, Georgia. "For people who can afford to leave it alone, it can be one of the best retirement accounts they're going to have."

In 2027, those with individual healthcare coverage through a high-deductible plan can stash up to $4,500 in an HSA, including any contributions from employers. That number goes up to $9,000 for family plans. Individuals can kick in a catch-up contribution of $1,000 if they're aged 55 and older and not enrolled in Medicare.

The HSA differs from the healthcare flexible spending account, known as the FSA.

FSA funds must be used by the end of the plan year unless your employer allows a carryover of up to $700 or an additional 2.5 months to use the money. HSAs, however, have no expiration date on their funds – and that's what makes them such a powerful tool for long-term planning. You can also take the HSA with you if you change employers.

"Get the money deployed, take advantage of the pretax contribution, and allocate the money into a growth portfolio," said Mark Stancato, certified financial planner at VIP Wealth Advisors in Decatur, Georgia. "With the HSA, you can keep compounding year over year."

The structure of an HSA and the available investment menu will vary from one plan to the next, and some will require that employees keep some of their holdings in cash.

Preset HSA fund menus tend to have 15 to 25 funds to choose from, and providers say that accountholders who invest tend to use two to four funds, according to Greg Carlson, senior research analyst for equity strategies at Morningstar.

How you allocate your HSA will depend on several factors, including your family's health prospects in the next year, your cash flow needs – how much you can comfortably sock into the HSA – and your risk tolerance, said André Small, CFP and founder of A Small Investment in Houston.

Small's standard is to keep an amount equal to 120% of the plan's out-of-pocket maximum held in cash in the HSA.

"That covers a bad year without forcing a sale at the wrong time," he said. "Above that amount? I typically advise investing the amount the client is comfortable investing, allocated to their risk tolerance, their time horizon and the goal of spending these dollars on care later."

For 2027, the IRS defines a high-deductible plan as one with an annual deductible no less than $1,750 for self-only coverage ($3,500 for family plans) and with an out-of-pocket expense limit that doesn't exceed $8,700 for self-only (or $17,400 for family coverage). Out-of-pocket expenses include deductibles, copays and other costs – but not premiums.

Other advisors suggest having up to the deductible in cash, though some HSA plan providers require a stated minimum amount in cash.

Beyond this cash reserve, financial advisors recommend allocating into stocks.

Patrick Swift, CFP and president of Amplius Wealth Advisors in Blue Bell, Pennsylvania, aims for an allocation of up to 60% in U.S. large cap stocks, 20% in small and mid-cap stocks and 20% in international stocks.

"We believe the equity portfolio should be well diversified," he said. "If the [HSA] balance is 2% to 10% of your net worth, why not be aggressive? That can change based on the situation, but if you are comfortable with the philosophical aspect, why not be growth oriented?"

Similarly, Stancato likes to go heavy on equity exposure in HSA accounts. "I allocate more dollars into small caps and emerging markets – those asset classes with more volatility but also more opportunity for growth," the advisor said. He also adds some large-cap domestic exposure.

For the adventurous, select HSA providers are offering brokerage window access, meaning investors can pick from a broader array of investments, including individual stocks.

This year, seven providers surveyed by Morningstar offer access to brokerage windows – up from four in 2023 – including HealthEquity, Fidelity and Lively. Be aware that there may be annual fees attached, either a flat dollar amount or a percentage of assets.

Rachel Elson, a CFP and wealth advisor at Perigon Wealth Management in San Francisco, recommends keeping things simple. "You can do a three-ETF model, covering some allocation that includes the U.S. market, and two ETFs for developed and emerging markets."

"You don't need to get super complicated here," she added.

#2716. NFL news, live updates: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III out for Week 10, per reports

The 2026 NFL trade deadline is officially in the rearview mirror, and we're on to Week 10, where we'll see a couple of players in new uniforms this week — and some in their old uniforms.

Kirk Cousins rejoined the Minnesota Vikings this week via a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. He will officially don purple this weekend against the Green Bay Packers after head coach Kevin O'Connell officially named him the team's Week 10 starter on Friday. He'll make his return to Minnesota against the very team he last faced as a Viking, when he suffered a season-ending Achilles tear. He'll look to give the offense a much-needed boost to complement Brian Flores' defense after the team's 6-2 start.

With the trade of Cousins, the Raiders officially named 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza as their starter moving forward. He'll face a tough schedule to kick off his career as a starting quarterback, with the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos on deck in Weeks 10 and 11.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more ahead of Week 10.

After a great deal of speculation was made that Jonathan Taylor could be moved ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Indianapolis Colts are reportedly standing pat.

The team will not trade him ahead of the deadline, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Tuesday afternoon.

Pelissero reported that the Colts had received multiple offers for Taylor of a second-round pick-plus, but instead, the team will move forward with him as a foundational piece within the locker room as they look to rebuild.

The Patriots added backup running back TreVeyon Henderson to injured reserve on Saturday.

This will sideline him for at least four games. Henderson has been sidelined due to an unexplained medical emergency that involved neurological symptoms. Exact details of what happened to Henderson are not available, but in a statement he released, Henderson said that things are positive.

The New England running back will be first eligible to return in Week 15 ahead of the Patriots' "Monday Night Football" game against the Kansas City Chiefs.

The Carolina Panthers announced Saturday that they've activated wide receiver Xavier Legette from injured reserve.

Legette, a 2024 first-round pick, has been sidelined by a knee injury, which he suffered in a Week 2 win over the Atlanta Falcons.

He could be available for the Panthers' latest divisional matchup, a Sunday road showdown versus the New Orleans Saints.

Legette is still listed as "questionable" on the team's injury report.

Montgomery practiced on Thursday and Friday, but will miss another game after being out since Week 5. Woody Marks, who has compiled 192 rushing yards on 52 attempts, will again be RB1.

Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III will not play in Week 10 after suffering a groin injury in practice this week, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Saturday.

Walker leads the NFL with 109 rushing yards per game and is averaging a career-high 5.5 yards per carry. He has seen a heavy workload this season, just 69 carries short of his previous career high for a season, despite being just eight games into the season.

Etienne has been on injured reserve since Week 4 after suffering a hamstring injury. The running back is in his first season with the Saints and has 128 yards on 30 rushes this season.

The Saints opened Etienne's 21-day practice window this week. After being limited earlier in the week, he was a full participant on Friday.

New Orleans is set to take on the Panthers in Week 10.

Barry Anderson and Duane Heydt, who normally serve as umpires, along with side judge Don Willard will take on referee duties on Sunday.

Anderson will officiate the Jacksonville Jaguars-Tennessee Titans game in Tennessee;; Heydt has been assigned to work the Carolina Panthers-New Orleans Saints game in New Orleans; and Willard will have double-duty first refereeing the Miami Dolphins-Indianapolis Colts game in Indianapolis at 1 p.m. ET before making the trip to Cincinnati for Sunday night's game between the Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers at 8:20 p.m. ET.

"Each of the league's 17 officiating crews have a backup referee identified, and that individual trains throughout the year to work at the referee position should the need arise," the NFL said.

According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero, Jacobs should return to action "in the next few weeks."

The Packers running back fractured his right ring finger last week against the Patrios. Green Bay has not announced a timeline for return. For now, Jacobs has not been placed on injured reserve, which would keep him out at least four weeks.

The San Francisco 49ers traded for veteran wideout Keenan Allen this week, but they're getting another reinforcement Sunday on the road against the Dallas Cowboys. Fellow receiver Deebo Samuel Sr., who has missed the past three games while recovering from a hamstring issue, has been cleared to play.

The Niners will, however, still be without Mike Evans. His Achilles injury will keep him out for a third straight game.

As expected, the Minnesota Vikings have named Kirk Cousins their starting quarterback for Week 10's matchup against the Green Bay Packers. That will mark his first start with the organization since 2023, when his season ended prematurely after tearing his Achilles (coincidentally, against the Packers at Lambeau).

It remains unclear who will back up Cousins in Week 10. Kyler Murray has been dealing with a hamstring injury, and Carson Wentz … well, he solidified the team's need to trade for Cousins in the first place with a disastrous start against the Buffalo Bills on "Monday Night Football."

New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr. was a full participant in Friday's practice, though he's still listed as questionable on the team's injury report with a hamstring issue.

Asked if he'll play on Sunday versus the Carolina Panthers, Etienne said, "I hope so. I definitely want to."

Pickens did not play during last week's win over the Colts and was limited in practice this week. But judging by his response to being asked if he'd be available in Week 10, the Cowboys wide receiver will be on the field.

Both player could return this week when the Patriots face the Lions in Munich. Brown traveled with the team to Germany and, along with running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), has looked "pretty good" in practice this week, according to head coach Mike Vrabel.

#2715. Warriors vs. Spurs player grades: LJ Cryer shines, Yaxel Lendeborg struggles

Well, that was not a fun game at all. The Golden State Warriors lost 123-85 against the San Antonio Spurs, in a game that was truly over before the Dubs even scored a point. They trailed 18-0 at the halfway mark of the first quarter, and with no Steph Curry to save them, there was never a chance on the road against a team that entered the night with a 10-game winning streak.

No one needs to spend much more time thinking about this game, so let's run through the grades very, very quickly. As always, grades are based on my expectations for each individual player, with a "B" grade representing the average performance for that player.

Note: True-shooting percentage (TS) is a scoring efficiency metric that accounts for threes and free throws. Entering Friday's games, league-average TS was 57.4%.

18 minutes, 8 points, 4 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 steal, 1 block, 1 foul, 3-for-11 shooting, 2-for-6 threes, 36.4% TS, -29

Melton got the start in Curry's absence, as I'm guessing he'll continue to do. He did some good things, but also some bad things. His inability to penetrate San Antonio's defense made it hard for him to quarterback the offense, and while he had some nice defensive plays, he struggled with the Spurs' speed and length.

24 minutes, 3 points, 7 rebounds, 1 assist, 1 block, 3 turnovers, 3 fouls, 1-for-13 shooting, 0-for-2 threes, 1-for-2 free throws, 10.8% TS, -40

Well, there's no way to sugarcoat this one, other than to say the obvious: these games happen to rookies, and they're just part of the learning process. Lendeborg will get better because of this game, but he sure won't have a fun time looking back through the film.

This was a double whammy for the Dubs' first-round pick. It was his first game since he was handed the keys following Curry's injury, and it was his first time facing a team like the Spurs. They don't make players like Victor Wembanyama in the Big 10, and they don't make defenses this long, fast, or rangy. Lendeborg was at a total loss when having to deal with those things, though credit to him for not slumping his shoulders, and still playing hard on defense and on the glass.

Grade: D-Post-game bonus: Led the team in rebounds; worst plus/minus on the team.

16 minutes, 4 points, 3 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 steal, 2 turnovers, 3 fouls, 2-for-5 shooting, 0-for-2 threes, 40.0% TS, -23

Green always feels like a barometer for whether or not the team can win. You can tell by his effort level whether it's a winnable game for the Dubs. He came out energized on the first few possessions, while defending Wembanyama, and then it became clear that the Warriors had no chance and Green's effort level waned with that. Can't really blame him.

22 minutes, 8 points, 3 rebounds, 1 block, 2-for-10 shooting, 2-for-5 threes, 2-for-2 free throws, 36.8% TS, -24

With Curry out for a few weeks at a minimum, the Warriors are going to turn to Lendeborg and Podziemski to be the first options on offense. Unfortunately, the first game post-Curry's injury was a bit of a dud in that regard. Podz didn't struggle as much as Lendeborg, but it was a very forgettable game for him, as he just couldn't find any spacing against San Antonio's length, and seemed uncomfortable all night. Props to him for not turning the ball over, though.

30 minutes, 7 points, 4 rebounds, 1 assist, 2 turnovers, 4 fouls, 2-for-4 shooting, 1-for-2 threes, 2-for-2 free throws, 71.7% TS, -27

You have to give Richard so much credit for being out there and playing heavy minutes despite his thumb injury. I thought he'd be out a few months, and instead he missed a single game. He also was not the problem for Golden State in this game, though perhaps he wasn't the solution, either. He was competitive, which is more than some of his teammates could say, and he fought hard on defense while making a few things happen on offense. It was the kind of performance that stands out when you win, but showed some limitations because they lost.

24 minutes, 20 points, 2 rebounds, 6 assists, 1 steal, 1 foul, 7-for-17 shooting, 6-for-11 threes, 58.8% TS, -11

Cryer was, without a doubt, the brightest part of the game for the Warriors. Maybe the only bright part of the game, for that matter. With Curry and Brandon Williams injured, Cryer — who is on a two-way contract — is going to get some run.

He looked the part in this game. He was part of the first group of subs, and immediately started doing what his teammates had been unable to do: penetrate the defense. Like all the Dubs, he struggled to score once he did that … despite shooting better than 50% from distance, he went just 1-for-6 inside the arc.

The 20 points was a career best for Cryer, and a reminder of what he's capable of with the ball in his hands. The Warriors will need him over the next few weeks.

Grade: APost-game bonus: Led the team in points and assists.

Horford didn't play much. Once it was clear that the Warriors were going to lose, there was no point in putting more miles on the odometer of the team's oldest player. He was fine in his minutes, though.

15 minutes, 5 points, 3 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 foul, 2-for-4 shooting, 1-for-2 threes, 62.5% TS, -15

Niang did some good things. He didn't do any great things, but he did some good things, and he didn't do any awful things, either. Just not quite athletic enough given San Antonio's players, and I thought his defense had a rough go of it.

21 minutes, 7 points, 4 rebounds, 1 assist, 1 block, 1 turnover, 1 foul, 3-for-8 shooting, 1-for-3 threes, 0-for-1 free throws, 41.5% TS, -7

Bassey's impressive play continued. On a night where the Warriors shot just 33.3% from the field, Bassey was the only player on the team to make more than half of his shots. He had some impressive rebounds as well. It wasn't all good, though, as San Antonio's size really got the better of him on numerous occasions. He struggled to contain anyone on defense, and the three turnovers and four fouls in the box score pretty accurately reflect how he played. But still: an efficient 11-and-5 in 20 minutes from the center position is something the Warriors are happy about.

Single-game individual plus/minus is perhaps the noisiest stat in basketball, but it still feels noteworthy — if not meaningful — that Payton was the only Warriors player to have a positive plus/minus in a game that they lost by 38 points. That's more a reflection of when he was on the court than of what he did on it, but still … worth noting!

GPII played some good defense though, which is more than most of his teammates can say. He wasn't a factor on offense, but then again, other than Bassey and Cryer, no one was.

San Antonio has so much length and athleticism that they were able to bother Ike with it, even though both teams had pulled their core players and put in the subs by the time Ike got on the court. Still, with the exception of a bunch of missed shots, Ike played fairly well. He passes really well for his position, and the game doesn't move too quickly for him. Did some nice things on defense as well.

#2714. Victims claim Rex Ryan "almost killed" them with truck in Nasvhille

The victims in last week’s Nashville incident involving former NFL coach Rex Ryan have come forward. And they are making specific and clear accusations about Ryan’s driving.

Via the California Post, attorney Michael Holland said that Ryan “almost killed” Holland and his wife with Ryan’s pickup truck, as they crossed the street.

“If we had been six inches further out,” Holland said, “I’d be in a hospital right now and so would my wife.”

Added Holland regarding Ryan: “He decided he wanted to turn and didn’t care, and just ran over both of my feet, my wife’s foot and got her leg too.”

Holland contends that Ryan didn’t stop, and that Holland caught up with the truck and pounded on the window.

“He was told in no uncertain terms what he had done, and instead of staying at the scene or even saying, ‘Sorry,’ he just got back in his vehicle and took off,” Holland said.

Holland gave the Post a photo of his wife’s injuries.

“I mean, just another inch or two, and his mirror or bumper would have taken off [my wife’s] knee,” Holland said. “His tire literally was like so close to her that it scraped her leg and ran over her feet and both of my feet. You just can’t do that. . . . My wife has already lost one of her toenails; I’m probably going to lose a couple of mine. Her leg is kind of scraped up . . . it hurt.”

Holland took a photo of Ryan’s red Ford Truck, with a Jets license plate holder and a vanity tag that says “HIT QBS.”

It’s entirely on brand for Ryan. Really, everything about the situation is.

Ryan faces six misdemeanors and is due in court next month. It remains to be seen whether he appears on ESPN’s Sunday morning pregame show.

Then again, with the Patriots playing the Lions at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday, it’s not as if anyone will be watching.

#2713. UEFA Nations League: Svensson scores first Sweden goal, Mæhle helps Denmark beat post-Ronaldo Portugal

Daniel Svensson helped Sweden to seal promotion to League A in the UEFA Nations League with a 3-2 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Borussia Dortmund defender finally scored his first international goal on his 20th appearance.

The 24-year-old opened the gates in the fifth minute with a difficult header from Anthony Elanga's cross. Sweden were 3-0 ahead at the break with a couple of successful penalty-kicks from ex-St. Pauli striker Viktor Gyökeres, but the visitors put up a great fight after the break.

Former Bundesliga players Armin Gigovic and Sead Kolasinac reduced the deficit within the first twenty minutes of the half. However, Graham Potter's side held on to their slender lead to secure top spot finish before the final matchday in Group B4. #2710. Castle, Spurs rout Warriors for 11th straight win

Planes were grounded nationwide on Friday night and the San Antonio Spurs grounded the Golden State Warriors from the opening tip in their second NBA Cup game. Fueled by Stephon Castle, the Spurs took a 20-point first quarter lead and never looked back as they defeated the Warriors 123-85 at the Frost Bank Center.

The victory is the 11th straight for San Antonio, who also improved to 2-0 in NBA Cup play and control their own destiny to advance to the knockout stage of the competition. The Spurs would need only one win in their next two Cup games to book a spot in the next round.

Nothing the Stephen Curry-less Warriors tried on Friday worked against the Spurs, who led by as many as 43 points in the game. Stephon Castle rebounded from a few poor outings in the last few games to score a season-high 32 points to go along with six assists and five rebounds. Castle shot 12-of-18 from the field as he scored 13 of the Spurs' first 26 points.

"He's in the middle of everything," Coach Johnson said of Castle. "He's an unbelievable impact player. He's never blinked at anything we've asked. He's never shown any poor body language. He just attacks everything. And there are times in this league, that is ridiculously difficult."

Early on, it was obvious what type of night this was going to be for the Spurs. San Antonio scored the first 18 points of the game and did not allow Golden State to score their first points until there was 5:54 left in the opening period. The Spurs' defense was swarming all through the first quarter, getting hands into the passing lanes and by the time the buzzer sounded to end the period, the Warriors only had 14 points were shooting 21 percent.

"I think the defense probably ignites the offense more than vice versa," Johnson said. "So I still lean into the defense. Thought we were pretty on point with some of our game plan execution stuff and attention to detail."

Golden State's standout rookie Yaxel Lendeborg struggled, shooting just 1-for-13 and ended with the game just three points. Credit to Victor Wembanyama and Luke Kornet, who both worked to make life difficult for the rookie.

"Nobody wanted to go into the paint," Lendeborg said. "Nobody wanted to get their shot blocked by him. So we were all just doing some weak-ass floaters. I don't know how many of us work on those.

San Antonio won all four quarters, but a 34-27 third quarter forced Coach Johnson to sit the starters and put his bench in with the Spurs comfortably ahead by 37 points. The majority of the fourth quarter saw Tarris Reed Jr., Carter Bryant, Jordan McLaughlin, and Keldon Johnson take the floor in mop up duty.

The win also saw the return of Devin Vassell, who missed the previous two games with adductor tightness. De'Aaron Fox was questionable with soreness, but he also took the floor in the win for the Spurs.

Victor Wembanyama had a quiet 12 points and 12 rebounds, but he was also hit in the throat, poked in the eye, and thrown to the floor by Draymond Green. After the game, Wemby commented on this and said he was "not surprised" by Green's flagrant foul.

De'Aaron Fox did not have his shot on Friday, going just 1-of-7 from the floor. However, he made up for that by doing the little things. He had five rebounds, four assists to contribute in a different way.

Keldon Johnson is starting to look like the man who won Sixth Man of the Year last season. He scored 18 points off the bench to go along with four rebounds and four assists in 25 minutes. If he can do that consistently, it makes the Spurs even more dangerous than they already are.

The Spurs (11-2) will now hit the road to face the Utah Jazz at the Delta Center for the final time this season on Sunday afternoon at 4 p.m. central time.

#2709. Tobias Harris Injury News: Return Timeline Revealed For Potential Season Debut

Fresh off their NBA Finals run this past summer, the San Antonio Spurs made a new addition to their backcourt: forward Tobias Harris. The elite wing scorer overstayed his welcome with the Detroit Pistons, leading him to sign with the Spurs for two years, $30.8 million. To this day, we've been waiting for his debut, and the moment may finally be in sight.

The 6'8″ NBA veteran initially went down during training camp after being diagnosed with a left calf strain, but the injury has gone beyond what anyone prepared for. Fortunately, as his recovery has progressed, a clearer picture of his timeline has finally emerged, with one insider claiming Harris could be back as soon as early December.

"Sources relayed to me that they [Spurs] did not expect this injury to linger on as long as it has right now," reported Chris Haynes. "But there is good news that I can report: I'm told he is getting better. Sources relayed to me that he is expected to start getting on the court for some practice work next week. If things progress, if everything goes as planned from next week when he steps on the floor, he could make his season debut as early as early December."

Hamstring injuries are notoriously tricky, and the recovery rates vary based on multiple factors. Still, Harris' absence is notably longer than the average, sparking some concern that his health might never be the same. If what Haynes says is true, then it means he's at least progressing in the right direction. Barring any setbacks, we could see Tobias Harris on the court as soon as next month, and it carries massive implications for the Western Conference hierarchy.

Harris, 34, is a longtime league veteran and naturally gifted scorer who can stretch the floor and create his own shot. After 15 seasons, he's no longer in his prime, but the Spurs believe he can still fill their hole on the wing, just like he did for the No. 1-seeded Pistons last season, when he averaged 13.3 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 0.9 steals, and 0.4 blocks per game on 46.9% shooting from the field over 63 games.

For a Spurs team that's 11-2, there's no use rushing Harris back. They're the hottest team in the league right now (11 straight wins) and coming off a ridiculously lopsided victory (123-85) over the Golden State Warriors. Sans Harris, the Spurs have done just fine with Stephon Castle and Devin Vassell on the wing. Off the bench, 25-year-old Julian Champagnie has provided a consistent spark.

So, yes, the Spurs may not need Tobias Harris to prosper this season, but adding his scoring and veteran leadership to the locker room will only raise their ceiling further. At the very least, it will add depth to their already deep rotation.

What can we expect from Harris himself? Probably not much, especially out of the gate as he shakes off the rust from an extended hiatus. Fortunately, he'll have all the time in the world to get his rhythm back and make a real impact for this red-hot Spurs team.

#2707. At least 50 different quarterbacks will have started games through Week 10

Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza will make his first career start on Sunday. Two others will make their debuts, too: Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck and Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord.

Via NBC Sports research, they’ll become the 48th, 49th, and 50th different quarterbacks to start games during the 2026 season.

It will be only the second time in the last 15 years (excluding the 1987 strike season) during which 50 different quarterbacks have started games in the first 10 weeks of a season.

If, for some reason, another quarterback makes his first start of the season on Sunday (that’s unlikely with Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock not having an injury designation for Sunday), it will be the second-most starters through 10 weeks since 1950.

In 1999, 55 different quarterbacks started games through the first 10 weeks of the season.

Most of the changes have arisen from injury. For the Raiders, the transition to Mendoza happened after Kirk Cousins was traded to the Vikings.

#2703. Highlights: San Antonio wastes no time blowing out the Warriors

There are good starts… and then there are very good starts. An 18-0 run to begin the game against one of the best offenses in the league qualifies as an outstanding start. The San Antonio Spurs built a 38-14 first-quarter lead over the Golden State Warriors on their way to a 123-85 win.

The Spurs were led in large part by the stellar offensive play of Stephon Castle. The guard is coming off a stretch of bad play, but turned it around in a major way against the Warriors. Castle had 32 points, 6 assists, and 5 rebounds. He had it going from deep, hitting a trio of three-pointers in the first quarter, and finished the game shooting 5-for-7 from three.

Castle did more than just hit open threes. The Warriors had no answer for his physical, downhill brand of basketball. With Draymond Green attached at Victor Wembanyama's hip, Castle and the Spurs guards got to the basket with little to no resistance at the rim. San Antonio outscored Golden State 56-to-28 in the paint.

Castle's passing was on point against the Warriors. He had no turnovers despite having the ball in his hands for a lot of the game. He was particularly effective on the primary and secondary fast breaks, where Golden State was slow to get back.

Castle and Wembanyama had the Area 51 connection working early and often. Wembanyama wasn't able to get free in the half-court too often with Green playing physical basketball, but San Antonio was able to get him a few lobs out of the pick-and-roll.

It wasn't just Wembanyama receiving lobs from Castle; he also delivered them. Sometimes it's easy to take this stuff for granted because of all the amazing things that Wembanyama can do… but this is your 7-foot-5 center dribbling the ball up and throwing an underhand lob to his point guard for a reverse slam. That is versatility in one play! Wembanyama ended the game with 12 points, 12 rebounds, 6 assists, and 2 blocks.

To further add insult to injury, the duo did it again just a few minutes later!

Early in the game, the Spurs ran a lot of pick-and-rolls with Wembanyama handling the ball, and their guards setting picks. The Warriors sent doubles at Wembanyama on these plays, making it easy for the guards to slip into the paint and create easy looks. Here, Dylan Harper is able to get to the basket and finish over Golden State's smaller defenders.

Golden State left the paint essentially wide open all game long. It felt like the Spurs could touch the lane whenever they wanted to. Harper carved up the defense with his tight handle for a nifty finish in the second quarter. Harper had a quiet but efficient game, scoring 9 points on 4-of-8 shooting.

Harper also nailed a transition three on one of the most memorable plays of the night. Shortly after the ball went into the basket, Green shoulder-checked Wembanyama into the ground and received a flagrant foul.

Wembanyama finished the game with seemingly no health issues despite the hard hit. He and the rest of the Spurs will get a day off before a rematch with the Utah Jazz on Sunday as they look to win their twelfth game in a row.

As Tennessee continues its push for an SEC championship game berth and a spot in the College Football Playoff, it may have to do so without one of its best offensive players.

Vols wide receiver Mike Matthews left the team's Week 11 game at Texas A&M in the second quarter with an injury on Saturday, Nov. 14.

#2697. Inside the Suns: Collin Gillespie, early-season player trades, the deep bench players

Welcome to Inside the Suns, a deep-dive analysis of the current Phoenix Suns team in which the Fantable — a round table of Bright Siders — give their takes on the Suns' latest issues and news.

Author's Note: All questions were sent out to the Fantable members before the Suns/Clippers game was played.

zenzino: We got these questions right after the Spurs game. My answer was 'yes, I am concerned'. Gillespie had a tough final 3rd of last season, and he kinda picked up where he left off. He's not bad; he's just not as good as he was the first half of last season.

The other effect of him not shooting well is he's passing up shots he should be taking, which sometimes leads to ill-advised passes.

I've seen some comments to the effect of 'he's got his contract, so now he's coasting'. I call BS. You don't fight through the things he had to fight through and call it good when you get your first contract. He's a competitor.

Over the last two games, it seems like he's finding his range more. It's only two games, but there is some progress. As the 3s go down more, his confidence will grow. He'll take shots he should be taking and hopefully hit key shots like we know he can. So, I'm a little less concerned now than I was at the beginning of the week.

Ashton: It is funny in that there are a lot of players not playing offensively well, so just to call out Gillespie is a bit hypocritical. Yes, three-point shooting is abysmal across the board, and Gillespie is not helping his case there. But look at Kennard vs. Charlotte. He went 0-for-5 from the perimeter as the Sun's backup sharpshooter but still carved a role out facilitating and making mid-court jumpers.

So, I am not overly concerned about Gillespie as long as he finds a role on the team as the games go on. And that role is to probably assist Booker as much as possible. Would a starter role help pull him out of a funk and make him consistent? Perhaps, and the season is still young enough to experiment with

OldAz: I think Collin knew you were asking this and intentionally broke out of his slump the last couple of games. But even before these last couple of games, he had one of the best on/off splits on the team among players that play significant minutes (behind Dunn, of course, who has one of the best on/off splits in the league).

Considering Gillespie plays point guard, I care much more about how the team plays with him on the floor than I do about his individual offensive numbers.  The same goes for Dunn, who really needs to start getting more minutes because the Suns play significantly better when he is on the floor despite his lack of counting stats. Really, this goes for all players, as it's far more enjoyable to watch Suns games when the team is playing well, rather than watching a "fantasy"-style game where individual stats matter more. As it relates to Gillespie, it was only a matter of time before his shots started falling. He is far too good a shooter to stay that low for long.

Rod: He did have me a little concerned until the Clippers game. Before that, he was making less than 30% of his threes and hitting on only slightly better than that from the field…and Oso had a better FT percentage (46.2%) than him (25%)! His percentages are way up in the past two games, which is a relief. Thankfully, his defensive intensity never left, and he seems to be back to having a positive impact on both sides of the court again.

zenzino: 'NOW' would be stupid. There is a reason there is no trade activity this early in the season. After December 15th, many more players become available for trade, so nothing will happen before then.

All these fantasy GMs are trade-happy. It takes (at least) two teams to trade. Another team has to want you; you've got to be willing to give up someone you want. These things don't happen easily.

By all accounts, a great guy and a better teammate. His playmaking has shown definite improvement, and he has bought into doing the things they're asking of him. Unfortunately, because he's being asked to do something completely different, he's not playing his game, and we're not seeing how good he can actually be. I've been a big proponent of giving it some time. But I'm not super optimistic. I think he can be a pretty great player in the right situation, and the Suns might not be that situation. I would love to see him excel, even if it has to be on another team.

Many fans didn't want him here in the first place. While he's been improving, it's not a steady climb. It still looks a little clunky. This is the first time he's been on a different team, in a different system, and having to adjust his game. That takes time, and I definitely think it's too soon to decide if he's going to work out or not.

"He's playing great. Trade him for picks while his value is high." Unfortunately, there's a subset of 'fans' who don't really understand basketball. I invite them to go be Lakers fans. They'll fit right in.

I have actually seen several posts saying it's time to trade Brooks. SMH. Fans can be a fickle bunch.

Should the Suns be putting out feelers after December 15th? Absolutely. See what's available. But it has to be a trade that makes a difference. They don't need to force a trade and settle for what they can get. There is no player on this team that is an 'addition by subtraction' player. If there is an opportunity to improve the roster, then they should definitely take it seriously. If nothing good comes to fruition, let it ride.

Ashton: Certain Suns players…eh? Gee, based on board comments, that could be literally anyone. Well, scratch Book. He is literally the only one carrying the Suns on his back. Of course, there are things to consider such as aprons and when players can be traded, but as far as I am concerned, I really do not think anyone on the squad, outside of Book, is untradeable. There has been a lot of focus on Green as the asset to be traded, but once that includes a pick, and don't even ask me what the status of Sun's picks is, nope. Pass.

This is my fluffy positive comment that some members on the board say is lacking. This is like a Back to the Future movie where the Suns are doing what they did last season. They are winning the games they should (Houston anomaly aside) and losing the games that probably would have. And to add more cheer to your day, the Suns still have the Kings four times and the Clippers another 3. Suns could be a play-in team!

So no, there is no need for a knee-jerk reaction quite yet. Particularly with the Lakers up next. I am still on the side of letting everyone gel together organically before the fans tear down the team and front office decisions.

OldAz: I believe they should be fielding calls from any team that covets one of the Suns "stars" (outside of Booker), but they also should not be hasty to move anyone just because they have gotten off to a slow start.  I would not include any young players or trade more draft picks, but if someone wants to offer the Suns a combination of expiring contracts, young players, and picks for a player like Brooks or Green, I would not hang up the phone.

Rod: Not really. Most teams aren't looking to make trades this early on, and I think the best return you could hope for might be an expiring contract or two. Giving up on a player this early sends a message to other GMs that you're likely desperate, and they're going to lowball the return they're offering (plus almost every team has at least one or two players that aren't available to be traded yet). Now if another team calls about making a trade, that changes the equation, giving the Suns a bit more leverage, and they should certainly listen, as it puts them in a better position to bargain.

And we have to keep in mind that the Suns have six players on their roster that currently can't be traded (Brooks, Williams, Gillespie, Goodwin, Kennard, and Ighodaro), which complicates things.

zenzino: Jamaree Bouyea. Hands down. Especially in a game like the Spurs game. I would have liked to see Jamaree in there in the 2nd quarter when it was obvious no one on the team not named Booker could get a bucket. What Goodie does for the defense, Jamaree does for the offense. He brings instant energy on both ends of the floor. And he can score. What he lacks in size, he makes up for in speed and energy.

Like everyone else, I'd like to know what's going on with Sheer. I know Ott wanted him ready for the Blazers game, but he hurt his ankle. It doesn't look like the Suns are going to blow out many teams, but they might get blown out more than we'd like. Still, it would be a shame just to see Sheer play in garbage time. It's hard for young players to get into any rhythm with that kind of playing time.

Ashton: Ryan Dunn only played ten minutes against Charlotte. Does he count? True, he may be injured, and that would explain it. The obvious answer is to give Koa Peat some run, if only to shut me up. It is not like Bridges and Brooks is setting the world on fire, so why not? Peat can clear a path for Booker while facilitating his touches. I mean, common, teams are now throwing triple teams at Booker. This is Koa Peat's time to shine in a role he knows well from his college days. I figure any other name to throw out there might be in the doghouse or incompatible with Coach Ott's thinking, but…there is that guy down in G-League named Drew Timme that could be elevated to the end of the bench role and utilized correctly.

OldAz: As noted before, I think Dunn has earned more minutes and fits well when multiple starters are on the court because he does not need the ball on offense and brings energy and effort on defense that the starters lack and can be infectious. However, he technically is getting some "rotation" minutes already.

The only real choices here are Fleming or Peat, based on their positional fit and long-term upside. I would always be happy to see them get a few meaningful minutes per game and expand those as they earn them. More important to me would be seeing current rotation bench players get more minutes when they are playing well, and mixing them in more with the current starters.  The Suns have been playing better as of late, so I would not rush to force minutes on Fleming or Peat unless they earn them, but I would totally be in favor of continuing to experiment with lineups and riding the hot hand (on offense or defense) far more than Ott has done in the past.

Rod: Here's my wild idea for the day…start Jamaree Bouyea at point guard and bench (or trade) Green. I really like the idea of Collin staying on the second unit, and Bouyea actually seems to be the better driver and finisher at the rim than Collin, and is also a little faster and more athletic. I'd just like to see this tried, as I think Bouyea could be a much better fit with Book, Brooks, Bridges, and Ighodaro (or Maluach) than Green. I don't dislike Green and don't necessarily want him traded, but I also don't like the idea of him taking a spot on the 2nd unit from any of the guys already there because they already play well together, and I wouldn't want to mess that up (which is another reason I'd rather keep Collin there instead of moving him up to the starting unit).

Second, Peat should start getting some meaningful rotation minutes soon. Right now, I wouldn't bench anyone just to get him those minutes, but if someone just needs some rest (or they have a hangnail, or the sniffles, or…I'm sure you catch my drift here), then sit that player and get Peat into the rotation for at least one game.

Finally, if there's even the slightest need for Oso or Khaman to sit out a game, activate Timme and get him some minutes with the main team. Sure, his averages in the G League won't directly transfer to the NBA level, but a guy averaging 32.5 ppg, 13.0 rebounds, and 7.0 assists while shooting 42.9% from three on 3.5 attempts per game sounds like someone who should get a chance to me. Reath hasn't been very impressive as the Suns' 3rd center so why not let Timme have his shot at earning that slot?

On November 17, 2000, Jason Kidd tied the NBA record for turnovers in a game when he turned the ball over 14 times in a 90-85 loss to New York. John Drew of the Atlanta Hawks previously held the record alone after committing 14 turnovers at New Jersey on March 1, 1977. This record still stands today.

On November 20, 1977, the Suns set a franchise record for team steals in a single game with 24 in a 134-112 win against an Antonio. That total is tied for the 4th most in a single game in NBA history. Starters Walter Davis and Alvan Adams both had 4, Paul Westphal and Don Buse getting 3 each, and Gar Heard finished with 1. Rookie Ron Lee had 5 off the bench to lead everyone in steals, though. Lee made a name for himself as a thief on the court and went on to set the Suns' single-season record for steals (225) the following season, as well as leading the entire NBA in steals that year.

On November 20, 2000, due to various injuries and declining performance, Rex Chapman retired at the age of 32. Chapman spent the final four years of his NBA career with the Suns averaging 12.4 points, 2.5 assists and 2-4 rebounds per game for the Suns while shooting 36.0% from three. He started 154 of the 224 games he played in Phoenix. He is 14th on the Suns' All-Time list for career 3-pointers made (324), 18th on the All-Time list for threes made per game (1.45), and 50th on the Suns' All-Time list of leading scorers (2,787 points).

#2696. Saints sent Jordyn Tyson to renowned hamstring specialist at University of Wisconsin

In 2021, the NFL awarded a $4 million grant to Dr. Bryan Heiderscheit and his team at the University of Wisconsin to research new ways to prevent and treat hamstring injuries. Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson may benefit from that research.

Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports that the Saints sent Tyson on two separate visits to the University of Wisconsin to be evaluated by Dr. Heiderscheit and his team.

Hamstring injuries have been a major problem for Tyson, who was out for three months with a hamstring injury before finally making his NFL debut last week. Tyson also missed time at Arizona State last year because of a hamstring injury, and he didn’t run at either Arizona State’s Pro Day or the NFL Scouting Combine because of his hamstring.

But there’s hope for Tyson after his evaluations in Wisconsin. Heiderscheit was able to identify a weakness with Tyson’s hamstring that he thinks can be strengthened with a specific workout regimen that Tyson has been following.

Heiderscheit previously worked with Packers wide receiver Christian Watson and helped him recover from hamstring injuries, and it worked: Watson has started every game this season and in nine games already has career-highs with 49 catches for 879 yards, and he’s leading the NFL with an average of 17.9 yards per catch.

That’s the kind of player the Saints think Tyson can be, if he can stay healthy. Heiderscheit’s treatment may be the key to Tyson staying healthy.

#2694. Class 4A second round: Miller, Colonels move past Tomcats: Covington Catholic builds early lead, advances to next round

ASHLAND Kiyan Miller literally carried the load for Covington Catholic Friday night.

The sophomore had 19 carries for 149 rushing yards and three touchdowns during a 57-28 victory at Ashland in the second round of the Class 4A playoffs.

When the Tomcats had a momentous start to the second half, opening with a touchdown and cutting the deficit to two possessions, Miller quashed the rally on his own.

The ensuing Colonels' drive featured five Miller runs, including a 28-yard gain while dragging multiple Ashland defenders downfield.

"It's who he has been all year," Covington Catholic coach Eddie Eviston said. "He's the guy that sets the tone for us. He does a nice job along with those guys up front. They allow us to be very balanced in what we do. We have some weapons on the outside and with our quarterback, but those guys get the much-needed yards"

Compounding the situation, Antonio Rodriguez put the home team behind the sticks on the next drive with a pair of sacks, and the Tomcats had to punt deep in their own territory. Jamir Kirtley collected a short kick on the run and sprinted away from the defense for a 45-yard return to the house.

Ashland could not escape an early 21-point deficit, but coach Chad Tackett hopes his team won't forget the fight and character they showed with their season on the line.

"I am super proud of them," Tackett said. "Our whole thing this week was empty your tank, and they did that Friday night. Our seniors did a phenomenal job leading this football team this year. I was proud of how we played. We played hard. We made mistakes, but we couldn't cut it close enough to get back in it. … It was a tough loss, but I thought the game was a lot closer than the score indicated."

Covington Catholic (8-4) opened the game with a scoring drive. The seven-play possession ended with Miller's first trip to the end zone on a 9-yard run.

Ashland followed with a three-and-out, assisted by a Jonny Lind sack. The Colonels wasted no time attacking with the resulting good field position. Quarterback Dylan Courtney hit Brandon Smith in stride down the middle of the field for a 45-yard touchdown pass.

"Our coaches did a great job of getting our guys prepared on both sides of the ball," Eviston said. "We knew they were explosive with their offense. Our defense did a nice job of getting a couple of negative plays early and put them in a third-and-long situation. It really helped build that lead."

Covington Catholic needed just one snap to score again before the opening quarter ended. Owen Pitzer found a running lane to the end zone on a 36-yard screen pass. Kirtley added to the quick-strike barrage with a short TD run in the first half. Miller supplied another touchdown to give the Colonels a 22-point lead at halftime.

"We knew he was a good back," Tackett said of Miller, "but we were really concerned about their quarterback and tight end. Those two guys on film were outstanding. Cov Cath's four losses are to Beechwood, Highlands, Indianapolis Cathedral and Elder, one of the top teams in their division in Ohio. And they competed in all of those games. We knew they were a good team. We just hoped that we could slow them down enough.

"We started clicking on offense," he added. "We found out we could run the ball and kept them off-balance with our passing game. I thought we moved the ball better than anybody outside of those four teams."

Justin Hughes caught five balls for 108 yards. He collected two TD catches, matching the Tomcats' single-season mark.

Tre Taylor had 48 rushing yards. Mav Ashby saw more carries late in the season after battling injuries for two years. He led Ashland (10-2) in rushing in his final game. Ashby tallied 62 ground yards and scored twice.

"He's coming back from the knee injury, and then he had an ankle injury," Tackett said. "We were using him exclusively on defense. The other guys got rolling, and we tried to get him back in. He's a great back, and his best football is ahead of him. He's going to mid-enroll at Georgetown and he will be an outstanding player for them."

Courtney finished 6 of 8 through the air with 151 passing yards for the Colonels. Mac Cogswell added a late 43-yard touchdown catch.

"We've always built our offense around getting multiple people touches," Eviston said. "The guys that got touches tonight did great things with the ball. It's good to see. It was a fun night offensively."

Covington Catholic's playoff path doesn't get easier, as they travel to Boyle County next week for the state quarterfinal. A convincing road win gives them added momentum.

"It's one thing we talked about," Eviston said. "We would probably be on the road most of the time. We talked about that mentality. It's something that we can't control. Wherever we go, we will kick the ball off and line up. Our guys did a great job of handling that mentality."

#2693. The Fernando Mendoza era marks a sizeable shift for rebuilding Raiders

By trading former starter Kirk Cousins for a third-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, the Las Vegas Raiders are turning to the top pick in the 2026 draft Fernando Mendoza at quarterback. The move from a 38-year-old veteran to the 23-year-old rookie marks a sizeable shift for the Silver & Black.

"Our expectation is for him to lead the offense, to lead the operation, and to go play a game here Sunday and be the leader of the team, be the leader of the offense," Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak said of Mendoza. "We have to prepare him and give him a lot of reps to get him comfortable. So, our expectation is for him to lead the offense."

Standing 6-foot-5 and 225 pounds, Mendoza brings NFL-size with a livelier arm and fresh legs with mobility to the quarterback position, as opposed to Cousins. But where the veteran has the rook beat is game experience. While Cousins may be a statue as a pocket passer, he did provide his younger counterpart an ideal mentor and sounding board. And Las Vegas is banking on the nine games Mendoza sat and watched Cousins operate provided a blueprint for the rookie to follow.

And what an opponent for Mendoza to make his first start against: The Seattle Seahawks.

"Like I said, this is a new experience. It's great. It's against a fantastic opponent. However, I have so much trust in the coaching staff, in the front office, and my teammates and the leaders of the team to go out there and best support everybody's 1/11th, so we can do our job to the best ability."

While Seattle is quite shaky offensively — ranking 18th in points scored and 17th in yards gained under rookie offensive coordinator Brian Fleury — head coach and defensive play caller Mike Macdonald has the Seahawks defense as one of the top units in the NFL.

If both Mendoza and Kubiak are to get the Raiders aerial attack on track this Sunday, they'll have to do it against the Seahawks' top-ranked passing defense which is ranked No. 1 in air yards allowed (1,396). Seattle is also allowing the fourth-least passing touchdowns (nine) and have racked up the sixth-most interceptions (eight).

Both the Raiders quarterback and head coach are eager to meet the challenge head-on, though.

"It is, yeah. And every week in the NFL is tough, and this is the best defense in the NFL," Kubiak said when asked about Mendoza's start against a top-tier Seahawks defense being invaluable. "And again, he's got to go do his job and not worry about a whole lot else. Everybody does their 1/11th, and everyone around him elevates their play."

Notice that 1/11th that both Mendoza and Kubiak were quick to drop during their respective times at the podium during media availability this week leading up the Week 10 matchup with the Seahawks?

Kubiak's offense epitomizes the all-11 approach. Ranked eighth in the NFL in points scored (238) and 15th in yards gained (2,979), Las Vegas passing game is ranked fifth in air yards (2,337) and are third-best in touchdowns (20). The offensive line — which has showcased much better pass protection ability than run blocking — kept Cousins upright for those 20 touchdowns and the expectation is the group doing the same for Mendoza.

The stronger arm talent the Indiana product brings to the table should pay dividends for Raiders pass catchers like tight end Brock Bowers (team-leading 48 receptions, 658 yards, and six touchdowns), fleet-footed wide receiver Tre Tucker (33 receptions for 529 yards and four touchdowns), and running back Ashton Jeanty (42 receptions for 371 yards and three touchdowns. Add tight end Michael Mayer (39 catches for 388 yards and a touchdown), and Mendoza has weaponary at his disposal.

Las Vegas' ground game is in the pits, however, and is ranked dead-last in yards gained (642) and yards per carry average (2.9). Much of this is due to lack of trench dominance and opposing defenses loading the box with eight defenders knowing Cousins presents zero threat to scramble and take off with his legs. Perhaps the Mendoza dynamic changes that for Kubiak's offense?

"But, hey, go through your progression, and obviously if it's not there, you've got to go run the football. And then when you're running the football, how do you protect yourself so that you can get us to the next down, because we need you available for the whole season," Kubiak said regarding Mendoza trusting his eyes, staying in the pocket, and run as a last resort rather than too quickly. "You're not trying to sell out for a yard on first-and-10, so it's an ongoing learning process. But that's also why when you're selecting men in the draft, you identify their instincts. I liked Fernando's instincts in college, and it's his first NFL game. So, we're all going to see. But I'm excited for his opportunity and just for the whole offense to go play together."

We're going to find out if Kubiak's quarterback-whisperer ways can transfer to Mendoza as it has with Sam Darnold (during the Raiders head coach's time as Seattle offensive coordinator last season) and Cousins.

While this game features the debut of Mendoza and matching up against Macdonald's defense, underneath all this is this simple item between the Raiders and Seahawks: Kubiak misses Macdonald's defense (Las Vegas' group is led by rookie defensive coordinator Rob Leonard and ranks dead last in points allowed (268) and yards yielded (3,469)) and Macdonald misses Kubiak's offense.

"Kirk has taught me a multitude of lessons, but two of the ones that stick out right now from your question is, number one, always being prepared and doing everything possible you can to prepare yourself to best serve your teammates, to best serve the organization. So you go out there Sunday, regardless of the result, no doubt in your mind that you did everything possible to give your team and teammates the best chance to perform and win. And second is to be yourself. He's always told everybody on the team, and he was a great leader and captain on the team and really brought us together and had a lot of togetherness. So that's something that I look to exemplify and take from his lessons."

—Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza on what lessons from former starter Kirk Cousins sticks out

#2692. Open Thread: Spurs and Celtics stand out in Emirates Cup competition

Last night the Spurs torched the Golden State Warriors. Until then, the two were the remaining undefeated teams in West Group C. As it stands now, each group has one undefeated team. In addition to the Spurs, the Mavericks and Timberwolves are 2-0 in their respective Western Conference groupings.

In the East, the Magic, Heat, and Celtics also have 2-0 records. Of the six undefeated teams, the Spurs and Celtics currently hold 53-point differentials. There are three more days of Group competition — Friday, November 20th, the following Wednesday and wrapping up two days later on Friday, November 27th.

From there, the eight top teams will be determined for the quarterfinals. The top team from each group advance leaving one additional spot. Those with matching records will organized by point differential. The Spurs and Celtics have a distinct advantage at this point in the standings.

The Spurs made it all the way to the Emirates Cup Finals last year. They knocked out the LeBron and Luka Lakers before upsetting the reigning NBA Champion Oklahoma City Thunder. They did fall short in the Finals to the New York Knicks. Although they outscored the Knicks in the 1st and 3rd quarters and tied the second, they unraveled in the final frame. The same issues plagued them and lead to their demise in the NBA Finals a few months later.

For now, the Spurs seem to have a handle on their competition. But there are always bumps in the road. Fortunately, this season, smoothing the edges has been a key to their success. Making adjustments in real time has given them separation in many games, even allowing a monster comeback last week when the Chicago Bulls started with an uncharacteristic 85% shooting during the first quarter. It is in these moments that the Spurs have been tested and shown they are more ready than ever to rise to the challenge.

The Spurs next Emirates Cup games is Wednesday, November 25 against the Portland Trail Blazers with their final game against the Lakers on Friday, November 27.

#2689. Recap: Wake Forest Decimates SMU 49-7

The Deacs have done it AGAIN. For a 5th straight game, Wake Forest has completely dominated their opponent, beating SMU on their home field by 42 points.

Stop me if you've heard this one before, but the Deacs basically won another game in the 1st quarter. SMU won the toss and elected to receive the ball, which turned out to be a costly error. The Wake Forest defense forced a 3 and out, and the Deacs quickly went up 7-0 in about 2 minutes on a 27-yard touchdown run by Ty Clark.

For a 4th straight week, a 1st quarter touchdown to take a 7-0 lead was enough to not lose the game. From that point on, it was just all Deacs—everything went Wake's way in the 1st half. The Deacs stopped SMU on a 4th and 1 on their own 26 yard line and quickly converted that into 7 points. Gio Lopez hit his favorite target Carlos Hernandez for a big 44 yard touchdown pass. Wake recovered an SMU fumble on the SMU 21 yard line—Lopez ran that into the endzone 5 players later. The Deacs even recovered the rare 44-yard onside kick when the Mustangs failed to field a kickoff. By the end of the first half, Wake was up 42-0 and had outgained SMU 248 to 120. That is just complete domination.

To emphasize just how dominant this Wake Forest team is, over their last 4 games, Wake is outscoring their opponents 145-0 in the first half. The Deacs were the first team since 2013 Alabama to score 20+ points in the first half and give up 0 points over a 4 game stretch.

The game was so out of hand, it was even booted from ESPN to ESPN News. I have a hard time believing that would every happen to SEC game, but the Deacs were winning by so many points it was really hard to be mad about anything.

I said all week this was a massive game with ACC Championship implications, and the Deacs showed up in the best way. It has been so enjoyable to continually watch Wake blow the doors off teams in the first half, and then relax and watch them coast to a win in the 2nd half.

Gio Lopez was maybe a step slow with that brace on his leg, but he looked really good in his return after sitting out last week—Lopez finished with 201 passing yards and 3 total touchdowns.

The Deacs completely dominated the line of scrimmage as well, outgaining the Mustangs 286 to 66 yards on the ground—Wake had more rushing yards than SMU had total yards (275). SMU's defense had no answer for the Wake offense, which punted just twice in the whole game. The Mustangs were so desperate for way to keep the Deacs out of the endzone, they even tried having the mascot poop on the goal line just before the 4th quarter. Even that didn't work, as Steele Pizzella, who entered the game in the 3rd quarter, scored on a 25-yard run right after the "accident." Thankfully, he was nowhere near where the incident took place.

Give a ton of credit to the Wake Forest defense, too—the Deacs completely disrupted an SMU offense that was putting up 37 points and 475 yards per game. SMU finally scored a touchdown in the 3rd quarter after a Jack Foley fumble, but Wake shut them out for 2 and half quarters. That included a goal line stand right at the end of the first half to block any chance the Mustangs had of gaining some momentum right before the half. Wake held Kevin Jennings, who entered the game averaging 307 passing yards per game, to 209 yards and picked him off 1 time. Hopefully Wake will lock down DC Scottie Hazelton the same way they locked down Dickert and Ezell in the coming weeks, because this defense has been playing phenomenally all season long.

With Duke, SMU, and Clemson all losing today, the only 2-loss ACC team remaining is Louisville, who the Deacs have already beaten. That means Wake Forest can clinch an ACC Championship Game berth with a win over Georgia Tech next week or Duke in 2 weeks. The Deacs have a chance to turn what has been an already incredible season into something truly historic. Wake should move up into the playoff field after thumping SMU on the road, but with the way the committee views the ACC, I won't hold my breath.

#2686. Ground stop nudges Ole Miss-Oklahoma game to Sunday (and OU doesn't like that)

Friday’s nationwide shutdown of the aviation system has resulted in a delayed kickoff for several college football games on Saturday. One of them was moved to Sunday — and the home team isn’t happy.

The Ole Miss visit to Oklahoma shifted from 4:15 p.m. ET on Saturday to Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET.

“The Ole Miss football team was unable to depart Oxford Friday night due to the FAA ground stoppage,” the SEC said in a statement. “After the stoppage was lifted, a late-night departure could not be accommodated by the charter company with which Ole Miss was contracted and the team’s departure has been delayed until Saturday afternoon.”

Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny strenuously objected to the decision to move the game to Sunday.

“After multiple conversations with the league office, Commissioner [Greg] Sankey informed us of his decision to move our game to Sunday, over our strong objection,” Denny said. “He further informed us that our failure to play on Sunday at the directed time would result in a forfeit. I understand that difficult decisions sometimes must be made under extraordinary circumstances. But those decisions must also consider the impact on everyone involved. Put simply, this decision isn’t fair to our athletes, our institution, or to Sooner Nation.”

Oklahoma nevertheless will comply with the decision. Even if the Sooners don’t like the decision to play the game later.

“Rescheduling the game has a significant impact, particularly on our fans,” Denny said. “Those who have made travel arrangements, accommodations, and personal plans around a Saturday game now face unnecessary disruption and hardship. Their time, commitment, and investment deserve greater consideration than they were afforded in the conference’s decision tonight. . . . We are obligated to play the game when directed. But we remain steadfast in our belief that the wrong outcome was reached this evening.”

On one hand, there’s no point huffing and puffing if Oklahoma ultimately wasn’t going to blow the house down. On the other hand, the school may have felt compelled to do something to deflect the frustrations of those who weren’t happy with having the game moved to the next day.

The bottom line is that the ground stop created travel disruptions and inconveniences for millions of people. And few are thrilled about that.

Oklahoma chose to complain. If it makes them feel better, fine. In the end, it doesn’t change the fact that the game will be added to the cluster of NFL games that begin at the same time on Sunday afternoon.

#2685. The NBA is all about fit. Paul George and the Celtics fit together perfectly.

We've all done it. We've judged players on various teams around the league based on preconceived notions and false narratives. We've jumped to conclusions based on what we think we know about someone rather than what we actually know.

That's human nature, and it's not our fault. When we see someone act a certain way once or twice, we assume they act that way all the time. Basketball mirrors life in the sense that one snapshot from the wrong point viewpoint can dictate how we feel about something or someone.

I'll be the first to admit that I was somewhat skeptical when the Celtics acquired Paul George. It wasn't that I didn't respect Paul George as a basketball player or respect him as a person. I did. It wasn't that I didn't think he could coexist next to Jayson Tatum. I did. It wasn't that I didn't think he still had anything left in the tank. I did.

But I didn't view George as a winner. I know he has made the Conference Finals three times, but I didn't view him as someone who could bring a team from very good to great and reach that next level.

I viewed him as someone who could put up stats with the best of them but those stats didn't carry much value, at least at this point in his career. I didn't think he could come in and seamlessly replace Jaylen Brown, play just as well if not better than Brown and help the Celtics maintain their perch as a true contender.

I was wrong. He can do all of those things, and he is proving it on a nightly basis. I feel like they should be printing out shirts that read: "I was wrong about Paul George" or "I owe Paul George an apology."

Every Seinfeld fan out there has enjoyed the Summer of George. Now, we get to enjoy the Season of George. He looks like a new man, both physically and spiritually, and someone who is playing with a freedom and purpose he hasn't had in years.

He resembles a player good enough to lead the Celtics to the promised land. I know, I know, it's only mid-November, and George has been injury prone throughout his career.

But, I think the Celtics have the right approach where he isn't playing every game. He looks fresh and is oozing with confidence and swagger right now. We all hope he avoids a major injury, but regardless of how it shakes out, let's make sure to enjoy what he's doing. George has gushed about the Celtics' culture, and it's clear the admiration is mutual as long as he keeps hooping.

George is the only player in the NBA averaging at least 22 points and 2 steals per game while shooting at least 44 percent from 3-point range. He has proven he is still a matchup nightmare who is fully capable of taking over a game.

That must have felt amazing to go into his old arena and light up the 76ers and take over a game that was pegged as a Tatum-Brown duel. On a court with those two stars, LeBron James, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey, George was by far the best player.

I could describe George's style of play in many ways, but the one that comes to mind more than anything else is smooth. He has a fluidity to his game that I personally didn't fully appreciate watching him periodically on other teams. Part of it is health, obviously, but part of it is natural ability that was on full display in his Pacers days.

George is reminding everyone that he is still a dominant force. He might not be as explosive as he once was, but he is still crafty, versatile and highly skilled. He makes smart decisions, defends at a high level, doesn't force shots, fits in with the Celtics' system and is clutch.

I felt similarly about Kristaps Porzingis when he came to Boston. The Celtics have a knack for revitalizing injury-prone players who have (somewhat fairly and somewhat unfairly) developed a mixed reputation.

George is back to his old self, and as long as he keeps this up, the Celtics are very much in the mix to contend for an NBA title.
